766.01 DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   "EMPLOYEE" means a person who performs any service or work for an
escort agency on a full-time, part-time or contract basis, whether or not the
person is denominated an employee, independent contractor, agent or otherwise
and whether or not said person is paid a salary, wage or other compensation by
the operator of said agency. "Employee" does not include a person who performs
services or work for an escort agency that is limited to repair or maintenance
of the premises of said agency or equipment on the premises, or the delivery of
goods to said premises.
   (b)   "ESCORT" means any person who, for any consideration whatsoever,
agrees, offers, or is held out to the public as available for hire, to act as a
companion, guide or date for another person or persons, to privately model
lingerie, or to privately perform a striptease for another person or persons.
   (c)   "ESCORT AGENCY" means any person who, for any consideration
whatsoever, furnishes, offers to furnish, or advertises to furnish, an escort
or escorts as one of its primary business purposes.
   (d)   "LICENSEE" means, with respect to an escort agency license issued
under this chapter, a person in whose name a license to operate an escort
agency has been issued, as well as the individual or individuals designated on
the license application as principally responsible for the operation of the
escort agency. With respect to an escort license issued under this chapter,
"licensee" means a person in whose name a license has been issued authorizing
such person to act as an escort within the City of Brook Park.
   (e)   "OFFER TO PROVIDE OR ENGAGE IN SPECIFIED SEXUAL ACTIVITIES" means to
propose or solicit to provide or engage in specified sexual activities for any
consideration whatsoever, and shall include speech, conduct or any form of
advertisement that would lead a reasonable person to conclude that specified
sexual activities are available in exchange for a consideration.
   (f)   "OPERATE" means to control or hold primary responsibility for the
operation of an escort agency, either as a business entity, as an individual,
or as part of a group of individuals with shared responsibility.
   (g)   "PERSON" means any individual, proprietorship, partnership, firm,
association, joint stock company, corporation or combination of individuals of
whatever form or character.
   (h)   "SPECIFIED CRIMINAL ACTIVITY" means any of the following offenses:
      (1)   Prostitution or promotion of prostitution; soliciting; loitering to
engage in solicitation; sexual performance by a child; public lewdness;
indecent exposure; indecency with a child; sexual assault; molestation of a
child; or any similar offense to those described above under the criminal or
penal code of any local jurisdiction, state or foreign country;
      (2)   For which:
         A.   Less than two years have elapsed since the date of conviction or
the date of release from confinement imposed for the conviction, whichever is
the later date, if the conviction is of a misdemeanor offense; or
         B.   Less than five years have elapsed since the date of conviction or
the date of release from confinement for the conviction, whichever is the later
date, if the conviction is of a felony offense.
      (3)   The fact that a conviction is being appealed shall not prevent such
conviction from constituting a specified criminal activity as defined in this
section.
   (i)   "SPECIFIED SEXUAL ACTIVITY" means any of the following:
      (1)   The fondling or other erotic touching of human genitals, a pubic
region, buttocks, an anus or female breasts;
      (2)   Sex acts, normal or perverted, actual or simulated, including
intercourse, oral copulation, masturbation or sodomy; or
      (3)   Excretory functions as a part of or in connection with any of the
activities set forth in paragraph (i)(1) and (2) hereof.
(Ord. 8434-1998. Passed 3-10-98.)
766.02 ESCORT AGENCY LICENSE REQUIRED.
   (a)   No person shall:
      (1)   Operate an escort agency without a valid escort agency license
issued by the City pursuant to this chapter.
      (2)   In connection with the operation of an escort agency, permit a
person to act as an escort who is not licensed as an escort by the City
pursuant to this chapter.
   (b)   Whoever violates paragraph (a)(1) hereof shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor of the first degree.
   (c)   Whoever violates paragraph (a)(2) hereof shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor of the third degree.
(Ord. 8399-1997. Passed 1-27-98.)
766.03 ESCORT LICENSE REQUIRED.
   (a)   No person shall act as an escort without having obtained an escort
license issued by the City pursuant to this chapter.
   (b)   Whoever violates subsection (a) hereof shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor of the third degree.
(Ord. 8399-1997. Passed 1-27-98.)
766.04 ESCORT AGENCY LICENSE APPLICATION.
   (a)   An application for an escort agency license shall be submitted to the
Brook Park Building Commissioner on a form provided by the Building Department.
The application may request, and the applicant shall provide, such information
as is reasonably necessary (including fingerprints) to enable the City to
determine whether the applicant meets the qualifications established in this
chapter.
   (b)   An application for an escort agency license shall identify and be
signed by the following persons:
      (1)   If the business entity is owned by an individual, that individual.
      (2)   If the business entity is owned by a corporation, each officer or
director of the corporation and each individual with a twenty-five percent or
greater ownership interest in the corporation.
      (3)   If the business entity is owned by a partnership, each partner and
each individual with a twenty-five percent or greater ownership interest in the
partnership.
   (c)   An application for an escort agency license shall designate one or
more individuals who are to be principally responsible for the operation of the
proposed escort agency, if a license is granted. At least one person so
designated must be involved in the day-to-day operation of the proposed escort
agency on a regular basis. Each person so designated, as well as the business
entity itself, shall be considered a license applicant, must qualify as a
licensee under this chapter, and shall be considered a licensee if a license is
granted.
   (d)   An application for an escort agency license shall be completed
according to the instructions on the application form, which shall require the
following:
      (1)   If the applicant is:
         A.   An individual, the legal name and any aliases of such individual;
         B.   A partnership, the complete name of the partnership and all of
its partners and whether the partnership is general or limited, and a copy of
the partnership agreement, if any; or
         C.   A corporation, the complete name of the corporation and the date
of its incorporation, evidence that the corporation is in good standing under
the laws of its state of incorporation, and the names and capacity of all
officers and directors, the name of the registered corporate agent, and the
address of the registered office for service of process.
      (2)   If the applicant intends to operate the escort agency under a name
other than that of the applicant, the fictitious name to be used and copies of
documentation evidencing the registration of the business name under applicable
laws.
      (3)   A statement as to whether any applicant has been convicted of a
specified criminal activity, as defined in Section
766.01 of this chapter, and, if so, the specified criminal activity involved
and the date, place and jurisdiction of each such conviction.
      (4)   A statement as to whether any applicant has had a previous license
under this chapter or other similar regulation of another jurisdiction denied,
suspended or revoked, including the name and location of the escort agency for
which the permit was denied, suspended or revoked, as well as the date of, and
reason for, the denial, suspension or revocation; and whether the applicant has
been a partner in a partnership or an officer, director or twenty-five percent
or greater owner of a corporation licensed under this chapter whose license has
previously been denied, suspended or revoked, including the name and location
of the business for which the permit was denied, suspended or revoked as well
as the date of, and reason for, the denial, suspension or revocation. A copy of
any order of denial, suspension or revocation shall be attached thereto.
      (5)   A statement as to whether any applicant holds any other licenses
under this chapter or other similar regulation from this or another
jurisdiction and, if so, the names and locations of such other licensed
businesses.
      (6)   The location of the proposed escort agency, including a legal
description of the property (i.e. block and lot), street address and telephone
number or numbers, if any.
      (7)   The mailing address and residential address of each applicant and
each person signing the application.
      (8)   A recent photograph of each applicant who is a natural person,
taken by the Brook Park Police Department, which clearly shows the applicant's
face.
      (9)   The fingerprints of each applicant who is a natural person,
recorded by the Brook Park Police Department.
      (10)   For any applicant who is a natural person, a description and
identification of the location of any tattoos on such person's face, arms, legs
or hands, or any other anatomical area that normally would be visible when such
person is on the premises of the proposed escort agency.
      (11)   The driver's license number and Social Security number of each
applicant who is a natural person and of each person signing the application,
or, for an applicant that is not a natural person, the applicant's Federally-
issued tax identification number.
      (12)   Proof that each applicant who is a natural person is at least
eighteen years old.
(Ord. 8434-1998. Passed 3-10-98.)
766.05 ISSUANCE OF ESCORT AGENCY LICENSE.
   (a)   Within five days of receipt of an application for an escort agency
license, the Building Commissioner shall notify the Brook Park Police Chief of
such application. In making such notification, the Building Commissioner shall
request that the Police Chief promptly investigate the information provided in
the application concerning the criminal background of the applicant or
applicants.
   (b)   Within thirty-five days after receipt of a completed escort agency
license application, the Building Commissioner shall approve or deny the
issuance of the license. The Building Commissioner shall issue a license to the
applicant to operate an escort agency unless he or she determines that one or
more of the following findings is true:
      (1)   An applicant has been convicted of a specified criminal activity,
as defined in Section
766.01 of this chapter.
      (2)   An applicant who is a natural person is under eighteen years of
age.
      (3)   An applicant is overdue in payment to the City of taxes, fees,
fines or penalties assessed against or imposed upon him or her in relation to
any business.
      (4)   An applicant has failed to provide information reasonably necessary
for issuance of the license, as requested on the application form, or has
falsely answered a question or request for information on the application form.
      (5)   An applicant has been denied an escort agency license or has had a
license to operate an escort agency revoked within the preceding twelve months
by any jurisdiction.
      (6)   An applicant is in violation of or is not in compliance with any
provision of this chapter.
   (c)   If the Building Commissioner determines that no other grounds for
denial of a license exist under subsection (b) hereof, the Building
Commissioner shall not delay approval of the application past the end of the
thirty-five-day period provided in this section solely because the Police Chief
has not provided the results of his or her investigation of the criminal
background of the applicant or applicants. If, after approving the issuance of
a license, the Building Commissioner receives information from the Police Chief
concerning his or her investigation which the Building Commissioner determines
to be grounds for denial of a license under subsection (b) hereof, then the
escort agency license issued pursuant to this subsection shall be immediately
revoked.
   (d)   An escort agency license, if granted, shall state on its face the name
of the person or persons to whom it is granted, the expiration date, and the
address of the licensed escort agency. All escort agency licenses shall be
posted in a conspicuous place at or near the entrance to the business so that
they may be easily read at any time.
   (e)   Whenever an escort agency license is denied, the Building Commissioner
shall advise the applicant in writing of the reason or reasons for such denial.
(Ord. 8399-1997. Passed 1-27-98.)
766.06 ESCORT LICENSE APPLICATION.
   (a)   An application for an escort license shall be submitted to the Safety
Director on a form provided by the Department of Public Safety. The application
may request, and the applicant shall provide, such information as is reasonably
necessary (including fingerprints) to enable the City to determine whether the
applicant meets the qualifications established in this chapter.
   (b)   The completed application for an escort license shall contain the
following information and shall be accompanied by the following documents:
      (1)   The applicant's name and any other names or aliases used by the
applicant.
      (2)   The applicant's date and place of birth.
      (3)   The applicant's height, weight and hair and eye color.
      (4)   A recent photograph of the applicant, taken by the Brook Park
Police Department, which clearly shows the applicant's face.
      (5)   The applicant's fingerprints, recorded by the Brook Park Police
Department.
      (6)   A description and identification of the location of any tattoos on
the applicant's face, arms, legs or hands, or any other anatomical area that
normally would be visible when the applicant is acting as an escort.
      (7)   The applicant's present residence address and telephone number.
      (8)   The applicant's present or intended business address and telephone
number.
      (9)   The applicant's driver's license number and Social Security number.
      (10)   Proof that the applicant is at least eighteen years old.
      (11)   A statement detailing the escort-related license history of the
applicant for the five years immediately preceding the date of the filing of
the application, including whether such applicant previously operated or is
seeking to operate an escort agency in this or any other jurisdiction, and
whether the applicant has ever had an escort-related license, permit or
authorization to do business denied, revoked or suspended. In the event of any
such denial, revocation or suspension, the applicant shall state the name of
the issuing or denying jurisdiction and the date of, and reason for, the
denial, revocation or suspension. A copy of any order of denial, revocation or
suspension shall be attached thereto.
      (12)   A statement as to whether the applicant has been convicted of a
specified criminal activity, as defined in Section
766.01 of this chapter, and, if so, the specified criminal activity involved
and the date, place and jurisdiction of each such conviction.
(Ord. 8434-1998. Passed 3-10-98.)
766.07 ISSUANCE OF ESCORT LICENSE.
   (a)   Within five days of receipt of an application for an escort license,
the Safety Director shall notify the Police Chief of such application. In
making such notification, the Safety Director shall request that the Police
Chief promptly investigate the information provided in the application
concerning the criminal background of the applicant.
   (b)   Within thirty-five days after receipt of a completed escort license
application, the Safety Director shall approve or deny the issuance of the
license. The Safety Director shall approve the issuance of a license to the
applicant unless he or she determines that one or more of the following
findings is true:
      (1)   The applicant is under eighteen years of age.
      (2)   The applicant has failed to provide information reasonably
necessary for issuance of the license, as requested on the application form, or
has falsely answered a question or request for information on the application
form.
      (3)   The applicant has been convicted of a specified criminal activity,
as defined in Section
766.01 of this chapter.
      (4)   The escort license is to be used for employment in a business
prohibited by local, State or Federal law, statute, rule or regulation.
      (5)   The applicant has been denied an escort license or has had an
escort license revoked within the preceding twelve months by any jurisdiction.
   (c)   If the Safety Director determines that no other grounds for denial of
a license exist under subsection (b) hereof, the Safety Director shall not
delay approval of the application past the end of the thirty-five day period
provided in this section solely because the Police Chief has not provided the
results of his or her investigation of the criminal background of the applicant
or applicants. If, after approving the issuance of a license, the Safety
Director receives information from the Police Chief concerning his or her
investigation which the Safety Director determines constitutes grounds for
denial of a license under subsection (b) hereof, then the escort license issued
pursuant to this subsection shall be immediately revoked.
   (d)   If an escort license is denied, the Safety Director shall advise the
applicant in writing of the reason or reasons for such denial.
(Ord. 8434-1998. Passed 3-10-98.)
766.08 FEES.
   (a)   Every application for a new escort agency license shall be accompanied
by a one hundred fifty dollar ($150.00) nonrefundable application and
investigation fee.
   (b)   Every application for renewal of an escort agency license shall be
accompanied by a one hundred dollar ($100.00) nonrefundable application and
investigation fee.
   (c)   In addition to the application and investigation fee required in
subsection (a) or (b) hereof, every applicant who is granted an escort agency
license (new or renewal) shall pay to the City an annual nonrefundable license
fee of one hundred dollars ($100.00) within thirty days of the license issuance
or renewal.
   (d)   Every application for a new escort license shall be accompanied by an
annual thirty-five dollar ($35.00) nonrefundable application, investigation and
license fee.
   (e)   Every application for renewal of an escort license shall be
accompanied by an annual twenty-five dollar ($25.00) nonrefundable application,
investigation and license fee.
(Ord. 8399-1997. Passed 1-27-98.)
766.09 INSPECTIONS.
   (a)   An applicant or licensee shall permit representatives of the Brook
Park Building Department, Police Department or other City departments or
agencies to inspect the premises of an escort agency for the purpose of
insuring compliance with the law, at any time that it is occupied or open for
business.
   (b)   A person who operates an escort agency or his or her agent or employee
commits a misdemeanor of the first degree if he or she refuses to permit such
lawful inspection of the premises.
(Ord. 8399-1997. Passed 1-27-98.)
766.10 EXPIRATION AND RENEWAL OF LICENSES.
   (a)   Each license issued pursuant to this chapter shall expire one year
from the date of issuance and may be renewed by making application as provided
in this section. Application for renewal shall be made no more than ninety days
and no less than thirty days before the expiration date. If application is made
less than thirty days before the expiration date, the license will not be
extended pending a decision on the application, but will expire on its normal
expiration date.
   (b)   An application for renewal of an escort agency license shall be
submitted to the Building Commissioner on a form provided by the Building
Department. An application for renewal of an escort license shall be submitted
to the Safety Director on a form provided by the Department of Public Safety.
The renewal application may request, and the applicant shall provide, such
information as is reasonably necessary to enable the City to determine whether
the applicant meets the qualifications established in this chapter. The
completed renewal application shall describe any changes or additions to, or
deletions from, the information provided in the applicant's initial license
application pursuant to Section
766.04 or
766.06 of this chapter. The completed renewal application shall be accompanied
by copies of any document or material submitted in connection with the initial
license application that has been revised or requires revision to reflect any
change in circumstances or conditions.
   (c)   The Building Commissioner and the Safety Director shall make
determinations concerning the approval of license renewals based on the same
criteria used to evaluate applications for new licenses under Sections
766.05 and
766.07 of this chapter.
   (d)   The Building Commissioner, in the case of escort agency licenses, or
the Safety Director, in the case of escort licenses, shall advise the applicant
in writing of the reason or reasons for any denial of a license renewal.
   (e)   When the City denies renewal of a license, the applicant shall not be
issued a license for one year from the date of denial. If the City finds,
subsequent to denial, that the basis for denial of the renewal license has been
corrected or abated, the applicant may be granted a license if at least ninety
days have elapsed since the denial was issued.
(Ord. 8434-1998. Passed 3-10-98.)
766.11 SUSPENSION OF LICENSES.
   (a)   The City shall suspend an escort agency license for a period not to
exceed thirty days if it determines that a licensee:
      (1)   Has violated or is not in compliance with any section of this
chapter; or
      (2)   Has knowing allowed an employee to violate or fail to comply with
any section of this chapter.
   (b)   The City shall suspend an escort agency license for a period not to
exceed thirty days if it determines that a licensee, or his or her employee or
agent, has refused to allow an inspection of the licensed escort agency
premises as authorized by this chapter.
   (c)   The City shall suspend an escort license for a period not to exceed
thirty days if it determines that a licensee has violated or is not in
compliance with any section of this chapter.
   (d)   The Building Commissioner, in the case of escort agency licenses, or
the Safety Director, in the case of escort licenses, shall advise the licensee
in writing of the reason or reasons for any suspension.
(Ord. 8434-1998. Passed 3-10-98.)
766.12 REVOCATION OF LICENSES.
   (a)   The City shall revoke an escort agency license or escort license if a
cause of suspension under Section
766.11 of this chapter occurs and the license has been suspended two times
within the preceding twelve months.
   (b)   The City shall revoke an escort agency license if it determines that:
      (1)   A licensee gave false or misleading information in the material
submitted during the application process;
      (2)   A licensee has knowingly allowed possession, use or sale of
controlled substances in connection with services provided by the escort
agency;
      (3)   A licensee has knowingly allowed prostitution, solicitation or the
commission of a felony in connection with services provided by the escort
agency;
      (4)   A licensee knowingly operated the escort agency during a period of
time when the licensee's license was suspended;
      (5)   A licensee has been convicted of a specified criminal activity, as
defined in Section
766.01 of this chapter, during the term of the license; or
      (6)   A licensee is delinquent in payment to the City, County or State
for any taxes or fees past due that were assessed or imposed in relation to any
business.
   (c)   The City shall revoke an escort license if it determines that:
      (1)   The licensee gave false or misleading information in the material
submitted during the application process;
      (2)   The licensee has knowingly acted as an escort during a period of
time when the licensee's license was suspended; or
      (3)   The licensee has been convicted of a specified criminal activity,
as defined in Section
766.01 of this chapter, during the term of the license.
   (d)   The Building Commissioner, in the case of escort agency licenses, or
the Safety Director, in the case of escort licenses, shall advise the licensee
in writing of the reason or reasons for any revocation.
   (e)   When the City revokes a license, the licensee shall not be issued
another license for one year from the date the revocation became effective. If
the City finds, subsequent to revocation, that the basis for the revocation has
been corrected or abated, the applicant may be granted a license if at least
ninety days have elapsed since the date the revocation became effective.
(Ord. 8434-1998. Passed 3-10-98.)
766.13 APPEALS.
   (a)   Any denial, suspension or revocation of a new or renewal escort agency
license under this chapter may be appealed to the Board of Zoning and Building
Appeals by written notice within ten days of such denial, suspension or
revocation. Unless the applicant requests a longer period, the Board must hold
a hearing on the appeal within twenty-one days and must issue a decision
affirming, reversing or modifying the denial, suspension or revocation within
seven days after the hearing.
   (b)   Any denial, suspension or revocation of a new or renewal escort
license under this chapter may be appealed to the License Appeals Board by
written notice within ten days of such denial, suspension or revocation. Unless
the applicant requests a longer period, the License Appeals Board must hold a
hearing on the appeal within twenty-one days and must issue a decision
affirming, reversing or modifying the denial, suspension or revocation within
seven days after the hearing.
   (c)   Any decision by the Board of Zoning and Building Appeals or the
License Appeals Board shall be a final appealable order, and the applicant or
licensee may seek judicial review of such administrative action in any court of
competent jurisdiction.
   (d)   Any licensee lawfully operating an escort agency prior to the denial
of a license renewal application, or the suspension or revocation of a license,
may continue to operate such agency during the pendency of an appeal to the
Board of Zoning and Building Appeals or to a court.
   (e)   Any licensee lawfully acting as an escort prior to the denial of a
license renewal application, or the suspension or revocation of a license, may
continue to act as an escort during the pendency of an appeal to the License
Appeals Board or to a court.
(Ord. 8434-1998. Passed 3-10-98.)
766.14 TRANSFER OF LICENSES.
   (a)   An escort agency license is not transferable from one licensee to
another or from one location to another. Any purported transfer of an escort
agency license shall automatically and immediately revoke that license.
   (b)   An escort license is not transferable from one licensee to another,
but the use of the license by the individual to whom it was issued may be
transferred from one licensed escort agency to another such licensed agency
during the term of the license, provided that the licensee gives written notice
of such transfer to the Safety Director within fifteen days of such transfer.
(Ord. 8434-1998. Passed 3-10-98.)
766.15 OPERATING REQUIREMENTS.
   (a)   No person shall, in connection with the operation of an escort agency
or in connection with acting as an escort, offer or agree to engage in, or
provide, any specified sexual activity for any consideration whatsoever.
   (b)   No person who operates an escort agency shall offer or agree to
furnish an escort for any customer, nor shall any escort act as an escort for
any customer, without informing such customer of the prices for all services
offered. In addition, prices for all services shall be prominently posted in
the premises of an escort agency in a location available to all prospective
customers.
   (c)   No person shall retain the services of any person under the age of
eighteen to act as an employee in connection with the operation of an escort
agency without verified, written consent from a parent or legal guardian of
such person.
   (d)   Every person who operates an escort agency or acts as an escort shall,
at all times, keep an appointment book in which the name and address of each
and every patron shall be entered, together with the time, date, service
provided and price charged. Such appointment book shall be available at all
times for inspection by the Police Chief, the Building Commissioner, the Health
Commissioner or their authorized representatives.
   (e)   No escort agency shall remain open at any time after 1:00 a.m. or
before 7:00 a.m. on weekdays and Saturdays, nor shall any escort agency remain
open after 1:00 a.m. or before 9:00 a.m. on Sundays.
   (f)   Whoever violates subsection (a) hereof shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor of the first degree.
   (g)   Whoever violates subsection (b) hereof, in connection with acting as
an escort, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor of the third degree.
   (h)   A person who operates an escort agency or his or her agent or employee
shall be guilty of a misdemeanor of the third degree if he or she violates
subsection (b) hereof.
   (i)   A person who recklessly violates subsection (c) hereof shall be guilty
of a misdemeanor of the third degree. Mistake of age is not a defense to a
charge under this section, unless the person under age eighteen exhibited to
the operator or his or her agent or employee a draft card, driver's license,
birth record or other official or apparently official document purporting to
show that the person was eighteen years of age or over, and the person to whom
that document was exhibited did not otherwise have reasonable cause to believe
that the person seeking admittance was under eighteen years old.
   (j)   A person who violates subsection (d) hereof shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor of the third degree.
   (k)   A person who operates an escort agency, or his or her agent or
employee, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor of the fourth degree if he or she
operates an escort agency in violation of subsection (e) hereof.
(Ord. 8434-1998. Passed 3-10-98.)
766.16 IDENTIFICATION CARD.
   (a)   The Safety Director shall provide each escort who is granted a license
with an identification card which shall contain a photograph of the escort and
the full name and permit number assigned to such escort. Such identification
card must be carried on the person of any individual while such person is
acting as an escort within the City of Brook Park and shall be displayed upon
request of any Brook Park police officer or other law enforcement official.
   (b)   Whoever violates subsection (a) hereof shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
(Ord. 8434-1998. Passed 3-10-98.)
766.17 APPLICATION OF CHAPTER TO EXISTING ESCORT AGENCIES.
   (a)   Any business establishment in operation on the effective date of this
chapter that is considered an escort agency under the terms of this chapter
will be subject to the terms of this chapter as of the effective date of this
chapter. Any such establishment must submit an application for an escort agency
license pursuant to this chapter within sixty days of its effective date. Any
establishment for which an escort agency license application is submitted
within the required sixty-day period will be permitted to operate, subject to
compliance with the non-licensing provisions of this chapter, pending review of
the license application and any appeal of a license denial.
   (b)   Any person who is considered an escort under the terms of this chapter
on the effective date of this chapter will be subject to the terms of this
chapter as of the effective date of this chapter. Any such person must submit
an application for an escort license pursuant to this chapter within sixty days
of its effective date. Any person who has submitted an application for an
escort license within the required sixty-day period will be permitted to
continue acting as an escort, subject to compliance with the nonlicensing
provisions of this chapter, pending review of the license application and any
appeal of a license denial.
(Ord. 8434-1998. Passed 3-10-98.)
766.18 EXTENSION OF TIME LIMIT FOR INVESTIGATION AND REVIEW OF LICENSE
APPLICATIONS.
   (a)   If the Building Commissioner determines that the volume of escort
agency license applications received during the first sixty days following the
effective date of this chapter is too great to allow proper investigation and
review within the time limit specified in this chapter, the Building
Commissioner may delay a decision on any or all escort agency license
applications submitted during the initial sixty-day period for up to an
additional 120 days beyond the thirty-five-day time period specified in this
chapter. If the Building Commissioner makes such a determination, he or she
shall promptly so notify the Police Chief and shall extend the time limit
specified for the requested investigation accordingly.
   (b)   If the Safety Director determines that the volume of escort license
applications received during the first sixty days following the effective date
of this chapter is too great to allow proper investigation and review within
the time limit specified in this chapter, the Safety Director may delay a
decision on any or all escort license applications submitted during the initial
sixty-day period for up to an additional 120 days beyond the thirty-five day
time period specified in this chapter. If the Safety Director makes such a
determination, he shall promptly notify the Police Chief and shall extend the
time limit specified for the requested investigation accordingly.
(Ord. 8434-1998. Passed 3-10-98.)
766.19 EFFECTIVE DATE.
   This chapter shall take effect and be in force as of the closing date of the
Settlement Agreement between the Cities of Brook Park and Cleveland that was
approved by the Brook Park City Council on May 21, 1997, by Ordinance No. 8323-
1997, and by the Cleveland City Council on June 16, 1997, by Ordinance No. 203-
97, as the term "closing date" is defined in the Settlement Agreement.
(Ord. 8399-1997. Passed 1-27-98.)
766.20 INJUNCTION.
   Any person who operates or causes to be operated an escort agency in
violation of this chapter is subject to a suit for injunction as well as
prosecution for criminal violations under
Chapter 501 of these Codified Ordinances.
(Ord. 8434-1998. Passed 3-10-98.)
766.99 PENALTY.
   (a)   Violations of this chapter shall be misdemeanor offenses punishable by
fine or imprisonment, as provided in
Chapter 501 of these Codified Ordinances.
   (b)   Each day that an escort agency operates in violation of this chapter
is a separate offense or violation.
(Ord. 8399-1997. Passed 1-27-98.)
CHAPTER 767
License Appeals Board
767.01   Membership.
767.02   Term of office.
767.03   Powers and duties.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Municipal licensing authority - see Ohio R.C. 715.27, 715.60 et seq.
767.01 MEMBERSHIP.
   The License Appeals Board shall consist of five members, of whom three shall
be appointed by the Mayor with the concurrence of a majority of the members
elected to City Council, and one shall be a member of City Council named by
City Council. Additionally, the Mayor shall serve as a member and Chairman of
the License Appeals Board. At the time of their appointment, not more than two
of the appointed Board members shall be members of the same political party.
(Ord. 8452-1998. Passed 5-19-98.)
767.02 TERM OF OFFICE.
   The term of all members of the License Appeals Board shall be five years,
except that the terms of the first members of the License Appeals Board who are
appointed by the Mayor shall be for two, three, and four years, respectively,
as designated by the Mayor at the time of appointment.
(Ord. 8452-1998. Passed 5-19-98.)
767.03 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (a)   The License Appeals Board shall hear and decide appeals from all
decisions made by the Safety Director with regard to any license that an
individual is required to obtain, under any provision of these Codified
Ordinances, to carry on a particular profession, occupation, or trade, or to
work as an employee in a specified type of establishment, where the regulation
requiring such license provides for appeal of licensing decisions to the
License Appeals Board.
   (b)   Within three days of receipt of any notice of appeal that is submitted
within the time frame specified in the applicable licensing regulation, the
License Appeals Board shall notify the Safety Director of such appeal. Within
four days of receipt of such notice from the License Appeals Board, the Safety
Director shall provide to the License Appeals Board a record of the decision
out of which the appeal arises, including the notice by which the Safety
Director notified the license applicant or licensee of the basis for his
decision, and any other relevant documents.
   (c)   Within five days of receipt of any notice of appeal that is submitted
within the time frame specified in the applicable licensing regulation, the
License Appeals Board shall notify the party bringing the appeal, in writing,
of the date on which a hearing is to be held on the appeal. Such notice shall
be provided by certified mail and, if necessary, by additional means designed
to ensure that the party bringing the appeal receives notice of the hearing
date at least seven days before the hearing date. Such notice shall inform the
party of his right to appear at the hearing, with or without legal
representation, and to present evidence and examine witnesses appearing for and
against him. The hearing date shall be set in compliance with any requirements
established in the applicable licensing regulation for the timing of License
Appeals Board hearings.
   (d)   The License Appeals Board shall conduct a hearing to determine, based
on the record provided by the Safety Director and any additional evidence
presented at the hearing, whether the decision of the Safety Director from
which the appeal was taken was consistent with the standards outlined for such
decisions in the applicable licensing regulation. The License Appeals Board
shall confirm the Safety Director's decision if it finds that the decision was
consistent with the standards outlined in the applicable licensing regulation.
If the License Appeals Board finds that the Safety Director's decision was not
consistent with such standards, it shall reverse or modify the decision in
accordance with such standards. The License Appeals Board shall issue its
decision in compliance with any time limit for that decision that is
established in the applicable licensing regulation.
   (e)   All decisions of the License Appeals Board shall be final appealable
orders. Each such decision shall contain written findings of fact upon which
the order is based, and shall notify the party bringing the appeal of his right
to seek prompt judicial review in any court of competent jurisdiction.
   (f)   The License Appeals Board shall in all cases comply with requirements
related to appeal rights that are set forth in the applicable licensing
regulation.
   (g)   All hearings conducted by the License Appeals Board shall be open to
the public, and notice of such hearing shall be provided to the public in
accordance with State law. In addition, notice of all hearings to be conducted
by the License Appeals Board shall be posted in the same manner as the agenda
is posted for all regular City Council meetings, and the License Appeals Board
may, by motion passed by a majority of its members, require the publication of
any hearing notice in any newspaper printed in the State and of general
circulation in the City.
   (h)   The License Appeals Board may adopt additional rules of procedure as
needed, provided that such rules are consistent with the provisions of this
chapter and do not delay the timing of any hearing or decision by the License
Appeals Board beyond the deadlines established in the applicable license
regulation.
(Ord. 8452-1998. Passed 5-19-98.)

901.01 EXCAVATION PERMIT REQUIRED.
   No person shall make any opening in or tunnel under any street right of way
within the City without first making written application to the Director of
Public Service for a permit to do so.
901.02 DEPOSIT AND INSPECTION FEES.
   Upon filing an application, the applicant shall deposit with the Director of
Public Service five hundred dollars ($500.00) to cover the cost of backfilling
the excavation and restoring the pavement to be disturbed, together with the
cost of any new material required. The applicant shall also pay a permit fee of
sixty dollars ($60.00) to cover the cost of supervision and inspection. The
Director of Public Safety shall issue a permit for the opening of a street
right of way only if such deposit is made and such fee is paid.
   The applicant shall also agree to pay to the City an additional fifteen
dollars ($15.00) for any necessary reinspection.
   Upon completion of the work to the satisfaction of the Director of Public
Safety , the balance of the deposit remaining after the payment of the cost of
labor and materials for backfilling the excavation and restoring the pavement
shall be returned to the applicant sixty days after completion of job and
approved inspection.
(Ord. 6129-1982. Passed 5-4-82; Ord. 9541-2008. Passed 12-26-08.)
901.03 EXCAVATING; BACKFILLING AND PAVEMENT RESTORATION.
   The permittee shall make the opening specified in the permit, perform the
necessary excavating and make proper connections, repairs or other work which
are required, after which he shall make the necessary backfilling to the
satisfaction of the Director of Public Service. Any pavement removed or
disturbed shall be restored in a manner and with materials acceptable to the
Director of Public Service.
   Should any person fail, refuse or neglect to do all or any part of the work
referred to herein, or perform such work in a manner which is unacceptable to
the Director of Public Service, the Director shall cause the work to be done
and the pavement restored. Payment for all work ordered or to be done by the
City shall be made from the deposit of the permittee. Should the cost of the
labor and materials involved exceed the amount of the deposit, the permittee
shall be billed the balance due. If not paid within thirty days after billing,
any balance due shall be recovered by legal action in the name of the City.
Failure to pay shall be cause for revocation of any other existing permits or
denial of any future permits applied for.
901.04 TIME LIMIT FOR COMPLETION OF WORK.
   The permit holder shall be obligated to commence work within twenty-four
hours from the date of issuance, and the excavation shall be made and all
necessary work shall be performed and completed within seven days after
commencement. However, the Director of Public Service may, in his discretion,
grant a time extension which shall be endorsed on the back of the permit with
the reason therefor. No time extension shall be valid unless dated and signed
by the Director.
901.05 WARNING LIGHTS REQUIRED.
   The permittee shall protect with adequate and sufficient warning lights and
devices any opening or obstruction placed in the street right of way. Warning
lights and devices shall be placed in such manner as to be seen distinctly by
all users of the street right of way at all times of the day and night. Whoever
shall neglect to perform the duty imposed herein shall, in addition to the
penalty provided by this chapter, be liable for all damages to persons or
property caused by such neglect.
901.06 OPENING PROTECTION AND BARRICADES.
   Deposits of excavated material or any other obstructions placed in the
street right of way about the work site shall be placed in such manner as to
insure the least inconvenience to users of the street right of way. The opening
and all obstructions shall be protected with adequate barricades during the
time work is not in progress. The Director of Public Service may require that
all trenches or other unfilled openings be covered by a metal plate sufficient
to maintain uninterrupted vehicular or pedestrian traffic and may further
specify the type and number of barricades as may be necessary to reasonably
protect the public against injury to any person or damage to any property.
901.07 WORK DESCRIPTION.
   The permittee shall provide the Director of Public Service with a written
description of work and diagram showing location snd addresses of street
openings.
(Ord. 6129-1982. Passed 5-4-82.)
901.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any provision of this chapter shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable under
Chapter 501 of the Codified Ordinances. Each day's continued violation shall
constitute a separate offense.
(Ord. 6025-1981. Passed 8-18-81.)

903.01 PLANS AND SPECIFICATIONS.
   All sidewalks, curbs and gutters shall be constructed, rebuilt or repaired
under the supervision of the Service Director and in accordance with the plans
and specifications, and materials prescribed and on file in the office of the
Service Director. As used in this chapter, the term "sidewalks" includes those
areas of land commonly referred to as "aprons".
(Ord. 7580-1991. Passed 5-21-91.)
903.02 NOTICE TO PROPERTY OWNER.
   (a)   Whenever Council deems it necessary to require the construction,
rebuilding or repair of sidewalks, curbs or gutters within the City, by the
abutting landowners, pursuant to the power granted by Ohio R.C. 729.01, the
Council may adopt a resolution declaring such necessity, which shall:
      (1)   Approve the plans, specifications and estimate of cost required by
subsection (b) hereof;
      (2)   Describe the abutting parcel or parcels of land;
      (3)   Set forth that the subject construction, rebuilding or repair shall
be accomplished by the requisite landowner(s) in accordance with the
specifications of subsection (b) hereof;
      (4)   Set forth that the subject construction, rebuilding or repair shall
be completed not more than thirty days from the date of the service of notice
required by subsection (c) hereof;
      (5)   State that, in the event the subject construction, rebuilding or
repair is not accomplished in conformity with the aforementioned prescriptions,
the City will cause such construction, rebuilding or repair to be accomplished
and assess the cost thereof against the requisite landowner(s).
   (b)   Prior to the adoption of a resolution under subsection (a) hereof,
Council shall cause plans, specifications and an estimate of cost of the
subject construction, rebuilding or repair to be prepared and filed in the
office of the Clerk of Council.
   (c)   Notice of the passage of a resolution under subsection (a) hereof
shall be served by the Clerk of Council, or a person designated by such Clerk,
upon the requisite landowner(s), in the same manner as service of summons in
civil cases, or by certified mail addressed to such landowner(s) at the last
known address or to the address to which tax bills are sent, or by a
combination of the foregoing methods. Such landowner(s) who cannot be found for
purposes of achieving valid service by any of the foregoing methods shall be
served by publication of notice once in a newspaper of general circulation
within the City. The return of the person serving the notice or a certified
copy thereof or a returned receipt for notice forwarded by certified mail
accepted by the addressee or anyone purporting to act for him or her shall be
prima-fade evidence of valid service of notice under this subsection. Such
notice shall also set forth the existence of the specifications on file in
accordance with subsection (b) hereof, the thirty day time requirement
prescribed by the aforementioned resolution and the possibility for the
assessment of costs pursuant to Section
903.04.
(Ord. 7581-1991. Passed 5-21-91.)
903.03 PUBLICATION IN LIEU OF NOTICE.
   (EDITOR'S NOTE: This section was repealed by Ordinance 7582-1991, passed May
21, 1991.)
903.04 CITY MAY DO WORK; COSTS ASSESSED.
   If such sidewalks, curbing or gutters are not constructed, rebuilt or
repaired within thirty days from the service of notice or completion of the
publication, as set forth in Section
903.02, the Director of Public Service may do or have it done at the expense of
the owner, and all such expenses, including cost of service of notice or
publication, shall be assessed on all of the property abounding and abutting
thereon.
(Ord. 7586-1991. Passed 5-21-91.)
903.05 PENALTY FOR DELINQUENT PAYMENT.
   Upon completion of such improvement the property owner or his agent, as can
be found within the limits of the County, shall receive notice of the cost
thereof from the City Auditor by registered mail or personal service. Upon
failure for thirty days from the construction of such improvement to pay the
costs in cash, an assessment with interest and a penalty of five percent, for
failure to pay within the time specified, shall be collected in the manner
provided by law for such improvements.
903.06 METHOD OF PAYMENT; MUNICIPAL BONDS.
   When sidewalks, curbing or gutters are constructed, rebuilt or repaired, in
accordance with the preceding sections, the assessment for the cost thereof may
be made payable in full not less than thirty days nor more than sixty days from
the levy thereof or in not exceeding five annual installments as Council
determines, provided that when any such assessment is in the amount of five
dollars ($5.00) or less, or whenever the unpaid balance of any such assessment
is five dollars ($5.00) or less, the same shall be paid in full, and not in
installments, at the time the first or last installment would otherwise become
due and payable. In anticipation of the collection of such assessments, bonds
of the City may be issued bearing interest not exceeding six percent per annum
and the proceeds used in the payment of the cost incurred by reason of such
construction or repair.
903.07 APPROVAL OF SERVICE DIRECTOR.
   No person shall construct, rebuild or repair any sidewalk, curb or gutter
without first obtaining approval of the Service Director.
903.08 LINE AND GRADE.
   The City Engineer shall set the line and grade of any sidewalk, curb or
gutter.
903.09 INSPECTIONS.
   Before concrete is placed in forms, the City Engineer or his agent shall
make an inspection of the work which shall be done to his satisfaction.
903.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any provision of this chapter shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable under Chapter
501 of the Codified Ordinances.
(Ord. 6025-1981. Passed 8-18-81.)

905.01 APPROVED CONTRACTOR REQUIRED.
   No person other than a duly authorized agent of the Municipality or an
approved contractor shall make any opening in or cut or remove any curb or
curbing in any of the streets, boulevards, avenues or public thoroughfares in
the Municipality. All curb cuts shall be made under the direction of the
Director of Public Service.
(Ord. 4130-1971. Passed 1-4-72.)
905.02 APPLICATION.
   Any person desiring a cut or opening in the curb of any street, boulevard,
avenue, public thoroughfare or downspout outlets, shall file written
application with the Director of Public Service setting forth and indicating
therein the location, kind and extent of the curb desired to be opened or cut
and the purpose and the size of the opening or cut which is desired or
necessary.
(Ord. 4130-1971. Passed 1-4-72.)
905.03 CURB CUTTING FEES.
   The fees for cutting such depression or opening shall be one dollar and
seventy-five cents ($1.75) per lineal foot of such cut for all purposes.
   Fees shall be tendered and paid at the time of filing the application. The
Building Commissioner shall promptly cause such curb to be cut provided the cut
can lawfully be made. Minimum fee shall be twenty dollars ($20.00).
   In the event an application is rejected, any fees tendered shall be returned
to the applicant within ten days after the date of rejection.
(Ord. 6125-1982. Passed 5-4-82.)
905.04 CITY CONTRACTORS EXCEPTED.
   The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to any person under contract
with the City who is engaged in the improvement of any street for the paving or
construction of curbs.
(Ord. 4130-1971. Passed 1-4-72.)

misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable under
Chapter 501 of the Codified Ordinances.
(Ord. 6025-1981. Passed 8-18-81.)

911.01 CONNECTIONS OF PREMISES NOT PREVIOUSLY ASSESSED.
   Where public sewers or water mains have been constructed and the cost
thereof has been wholly or partly paid out of the funds of the City or financed
through the issuance of bonds, and the owner of any property abutting upon such
sewers or water mains makes application to tap such sewers or water mains, no
permit shall be issued to such abutting property owner to make such connection,
nor shall such abutting property owner make such connection, unless he shall
have first paid to the City, or given security for such payment satisfactory to
the City Auditor, that portion of the cost of such sewers or water mains which
the property of such owner, for which connections are desired to be made, was
formerly charged in the form of an assessment, but which assessment the City
has been unable to collect due to defects in procedure or the failure to obtain
an assessment lien for such cost. However, where a portion of the cost of such
sewers or water mains to which connections are desired to be made has been
assessed against such abutting property and a valid assessment lien imposed
thereon for such cost, or where in the case of an invalid assessment, a
reassessment for such cost may be levied under and by authority of Ohio R. C.
727.39, such permit shall be issued, provided the same conforms with the other
regulations of the City.
(Ord. 1640-1956. Passed 5-1-56.)

913.01 CONNECTION PERMIT REQUIRED.
   No person shall make any connection to the water mains or distribution pipes
located within the City unless he shall obtain a water tap permit from the Fire
Chief. No connection or tap shall be made except by personnel of the Cleveland
Water Department or persons authorized to do such work.
(Ord. 4553-1974. Passed 3-19-74.)
913.02 HYDRANT USE; PERMIT AND DAMAGE; FEE.
   No person, other than members of the City Safety and Service Departments,
shall tamper with or in any way use a fire hydrant in the City unless he shall
first obtain a permit from the Fire Department and pay a fee of twenty-five
dollars ($25.00) to cover the cost of supervision and inspection.
   he permittee shall be liable to the City for any damage to such hydrant. The
permittee shall notify the Fire Department when the hydrant is shut off, and
the Fire Department shall determine if any damage has been done. If the Fire
Department ascertains that damage has been done, they shall so advise the
permittee by registered mail and, if such damage is not corrected, the
permittee shall be fully subject to the penalty provisions of Section
913.99.
(Ord. 7137-1988. Passed 4-5-88.)
913.03 OBSTRUCTING OR DAMAGING WATER FIXTURES.
   No person shall place or deposit any dirt or material in any fire hydrant or
in any valve box or stop cock, or commit any act tending to obstruct the use
thereof, or injure in any manner any fixture connected with the water system of
the City.
(Ord. 623. Passed 4-6-31.)
913.04 UNAUTHORIZED INTERFERENCE OR CONNECTIONS.
   No person shall maliciously open, close, adjust or interfere with a fire
hydrant, valve, regulator, gauge, gate, disc, curb cock, stop cock, meter or
other regulator, operating or measuring device or appliance in or attached to
the wells, tanks, reservoirs, conduits, pipes, mains, service pipes, house
pipes or other pipes or apparatus of the City water system with intent to cause
the escape of water or to injure or destroy such property. No person shall tap,
sever, open or make unauthorized connections with a main or pipe used or
intended for the transmission of water. This section does not apply to any City
agent or employee for that purpose or to anything done by or under authority of
the City Fire Department.
(ORC 4933.22)
913.05 WATER SPRINKLING BAN.
   (a)   Whenever the City of Cleveland, Division of Water, issues any
directive to the public to conserve water, or, at any time that the Brook Park
Director of Public Safety determines that a significant water shortage exists
in the City of Brook Park, a public water emergency is declared to exist.
   (b)   Whenever such an emergency exists, the Brook Park Director of Public
Safety shall request the cooperation of the local press, radio and television
stations to announce the emergency and the time that emergency use regulations
will become effective. Such emergency use regulations shall become effective no
sooner than one hour after the first announcement. Such announcement by two
local radio stations, or two local television stations, or in a daily newspaper
of general circulation in the City, shall constitute notice to the general
public of the existence of the emergency. The emergency shall continue until
announcement by the Brook Park Director of Public Safety or the City of
Cleveland, Division of Water, that the emergency has ceased to exist. Such
announcement that the emergency has ceased to exist shall be made in the same
manner as outlined above: two local radio stations, or two local television
stations, or in a daily newspaper of general circulation in the City.
   (c)   During the period of emergency, the Brook Park Director of Public
Safety may prohibit the use of any water for the sprinkling or irrigation of
lawns and/or gardens and for the washing of motor vehicles and the filling of
swimming pools. The Brook Park Director of Public Safety may also prohibit any
use of water for other than drinking and sanitation purposes. The prohibited
uses shall be specified in the announcement of the public water emergency.
   (d)   Whoever violates such emergency use regulation shall be deemed guilty
of misconduct at an emergency and shall be punished pursuant to Section
509.05(c) of the General Offenses Code.
(Ord. 7177-1988. Passed 9-6-88.)
913.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any provision of this chapter, except as otherwise
specifically provided for, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor of the first
degree, punishable under Chapter
501 of the Codified Ordinances.
(Ord. 6025-1981. Passed 8-18-81.)

915.01 CONNECTION PERMIT REQUIRED; FEE.
   No building sewer or drain shall be constructed to connect with a public
storm sewer, nor shall any connection be made to a public storm sewer within
the City until a permit from the Service Director has been obtained by the
person, firm or corporation proposing to or employed to perform the work. An
application for a permit shall be signed by the owner, lessee or agent of the
property for which the connection is desired and by the person, firm or
corporation employed to perform the work, and must describe the property for
which the connection is desired. The application shall be accompanied by a
permit fee in the amount of twenty dollars ($20.00) to cover the cost of
supervision and inspection.
(Ord. 7143-1988. Passed 4-19-88.)
915.02 TYPE DISCHARGE ALLOWED AND PROHIBITED.
   Permission to construct or connect a building sewer or drain connection with
a public storm sewer shall be governed by the following requirements:
   Such building sewer or drain may be used for the removal of surface water,
rain water from roofs, subsoil drainage, building foundation drainage, cistern
overflow, clear water from condensers, waste water from water motors and
elevators and any other clean and unobjectionable waste water. Such building
sewer or drain shall not receive sewage, floor drainage, industrial wastes,
septic tank overflow, cesspool overflow, privy vault drainage, kitchen wastes
or any other liquid wastes of objectionable character. 
(Ord. 473. Passed 10-7-29.)
915.03 INSPECTION PRIOR TO COVERING OR USE.
   After a building sewer or drain to connect with a public storm sewer is
laid, and before it is covered or used, it shall be inspected and approved by
the Service Director or his authorized agent.
(Ord. 473. Passed 10-7-29.)
915.04 REGULATIONS AND RECORDS; REMOVAL OF UNLAWFUL CONNECTIONS.
   The Service Director is authorized to adopt and enforce specifications and
regulations in accordance with the provisions of this chapter for the purpose
of providing control of the installation of storm sewer connections and the
inspection thereof. The Director shall maintain accurate and complete records
of all permits issued and inspections made. The Director is hereby empowered to
require the abandonment and removal of connections to the public storm sewers
which violate the provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. 473. Passed 10-7-29.)
915.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any provision of this chapter shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable under
Chapter 501 of the Codified Ordinances.
(Ord. 6025-1981. Passed 8-18-81.)
CHAPTER 916
Illicit Discharge and Illegal Connection Control

916.02   Purpose and scope.
