which does not have a sprinkler system or other similar fire detection system.
Every sprinkler system or other similar fire detection shall be approved and a
permit issued therefore by the Fire Department.
(Ord. 5985-1981. Passed 6-8-81.)
1302.21 SECURITY ILLUMINATION REQUIREMENTS.
   The following illumination provisions shall be applicable to all future
condominium and conversion condominium developments within the City and
existing development within six months of the effective date of this section.
   (a)   Definitions. The following definitions shall be applicable to this
section.
      (1)   "One footcandle" means the amount of illumination provided by one
lumen uniformly distributed on one square foot of surface.
      (2)   "Illumination source" means a device, such as a lamp, which
produces visible energy as distinguished from devices or bodies which reflect
or transmit light such as a luminaire.
      (3)   "Lumen" means the quantity of luminous flux intercepted by a
surface of one square foot, all points of which are one foot from a uniform
source of one candela. A one candela source provides 12.57 lumens or one lumen
per square foot of surface on a sphere having a radius of one foot.
      (4)   Metering equipment. Illumination levels shall be measured in foot-
candles with a direct reading portable light meter with a color and cosine
corrected sensor with multiple scales. The meter shall read with an accuracy of
fifteen percent (15%) . It shall have been tested and calibrated by an
independent commercial photometric laboratory or the manufacturer within one
year of date of use as attested to by certificate issued by such laboratory.
      (5)   Method of measurement. The meter sensor shall be mounted not more
than six inches above finished grade in a horizontal position. Reading shall be
taken by qualified personnel only after the cell has been exposed long enough
to provide a constant reading. Measurements shall be made at least one-half
hour after sunset upon the existing questioned light sources.
      (6)   "Exterior walkways" means the paved pedestrian areas, including
steps, defined by the building owner, and approved by the Building Department,
as the primary paths used by occupants for access to the building.
      (7)   "Exterior steps" means steps consisting of one or more risers that
are part of the exterior walkways.
      (8)   "Entrances" means all means of access to the main building by
occupants and/or visitors.
      (9)   "Parking lots" means all exterior areas where owners, tenants or
visitors normally park vehicles.
      (10)   "Parking garage" means a building or portion of a building
designed for and used for the temporary storage of passenger automobiles, and/
or recreational vehicles.
   (b)   Exterior Walkways. All exterior walkways in excess of twenty feet in
length shall be illuminated from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour
before sunrise to an illumination level measured at any point along the walkway
of not less than two-tenths footcandle maintained.
   (c)   Exterior Steps. All exterior steps that are part of the exterior
walkways more than twenty feet from the pedestrian entrance to the building
shall be illuminated from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before
sunrise to a level at least double that of the illumination level measured ten
feet in either direction along the walkway adjacent to the steps. The
illumination level at the steps must be minimum of four-tenths footcandle
maintained.
   (d)   Entrances. All entrances to each building shall be illuminated from
one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise with an illumination
source located within five feet of the doorway of not less than two footcandles
maintained immediately below the illumination source six inches above finished
grade with a minimum of one footcandle maintained measured at the horizontal
surface immediately in front of the center of the doorway.
   (e)   Parking Lots. All outside parking areas shall be illuminated from one-
half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise to an illumination level
measured at any point in the paved area of the parking lot or driveways, when
unobstructed, of not less than two-tenths footcandle maintained.
   (f)   Parking Garages. All parking shall be illuminated at all times to a
level measured anywhere in the unobstructed parking area of not less than six-
tenths footcandle maintained, and measured anywhere along aisleways for
movement of vehicles, of not less than two footcandles maintained.
   All illumination requirements contained herein shall be designed and
shielded so as not to shine, glare, reflect or be directed into or towards any
premises used for residential purposes.
   All illumination requirements contained herein are the minimum and shall be
maintained at all times as indicated.
(Ord. 5985-1981. Passed 6-8-81.)
1302.22 PROHIBITIONS AGAINST UNLAWFUL REPRESENTATIONS.
   (a)   General. It shall be unlawful for any developer or agent selling or
offering to sell any condominium unit in any condominium development to:
      (1)   Employ any device, scheme or artifice to defraud;
      (2)   Obtain money or property by means of any untrue statement of a
material fact or by an omission to state a material fact necessary in order to
make the statements made not misleading or by any pictorial representations
which are false;
      (3)   Engage in any transaction, practice or course of business which
operates or would operate as a fraud or deceit upon a purchaser;
      (4)   Make or cause to be made in any document required by this chapter
any statement or representation that is knowingly false or misleading; or
      (5)   Make or cause to be made to any purchaser any oral representation
which differs from the statements made in any document required by this
chapter.
   (b)   Specific. It shall be unlawful for any developer or agent in selling
or offering to sell any condominium unit in any condominium development to:
      (1)   Request a tenant and/or purchaser to acknowledge receipt of any
notice or public offering statement which he has not received, or to falsify
the date of receipt;
      (2)   Certify falsely to having provided notices of the public offering
statement required by this chapter; or
      (3)   Apply undue pressure to induce a tenant to purchase a unit which
intrudes on or prevents his use of his best judgment in deciding whether to
purchase, including the following:
         A.   Any direct or indirect increase or decrease in the purchase price
or benefits offered to tenants during any portion of the period during which
the tenants are entitled to a right of first refusal pursuant to Section
1302.19(h).
         B.   Any false statements as to the number of standby or backup sales
contracts or reservations or subscriptions or like agreements.
         C.   Any false statement prior to the end of the period during which
the tenant may not be evicted without cause pursuant to Section
1302.19(h) as to a future rent increase.
         D.   Any false statement relating to future conversations which would
reduce rental units available in the City.
(Ord. 5985-1981. Passed 6-8-81.)
1302.23 EQUAL OPPORTUNITY.
   No person shall be denied the right to purchase or lease a condominium unit
in the City because of race, color, creed, sex, religious beliefs, national
origin or handicap .
(Ord . 5985-1981. Passed 6-8-81. )
1302.24 REMEDIES.
   (a)   Public's Remedies.
      (1)   The rights, obligations and remedies set forth in this chapter
shall be cumulative and in addition to any others available at law or in
equity.
      (2)   The City or any tenant, purchaser or owner of a unit may seek
compliance of any provision of this chapter in a court of competent
jurisdiction, provided, however, that only the City may enforce the provisions
of subsection (b) hereof.
      (3)   In any action brought to enforce any provision of this chapter
except subsection (b) hereof a prevailing plaintiff shall be entitled to
recover, in addition to any other remedy available, his reasonable attorney's
fees.
      (4)   If a developer fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter, a purchaser may at his option at any time prior to the closing of the
sale rescind, in writing, the contract of sale, without any liability on the
part of the purchaser and shall thereupon be entitled to the return of the
moneys made on account of the contract, and any expenses incurred on account of
the contract shall be the responsibility of the developer.
   (b)   City's Remedies. Whenever it is determined by the Director of Law that
there has been a violation of this chapter, the Law Department is authorized,
at its discretion, to commence with one or more of the following:
      (1)   Attempt to conciliate the matter by conference or otherwise and
secure a written conciliation agreement;
      (2)   Seek a written assurance of discontinuance which shall be signed by
the developer and the Director of Law;
      (3)   Institute injunctive or other appropriate action or proceeding in
any court of competent jurisdiction to obtain a restraining order, permanent or
temporary injunction or any other appropriate form of relief; or
      (4)   Institute criminal proceedings.
(Ord. 5985-1981. Passed 6-8-81.)
1302.99 PENALTY.
   (a)   Any person found guilty of violating any of the provisions of this
chapter upon conviction thereof shall be guilty of a misdemeanor of the second
degree for the first offense and for a second or subsequent offense shall be
guilty of a misdemeanor of the first degree.
   (b)   Each day such violation occurs or continues shall constitute a
separate offense.
   (c)   Violation of any provision of this chapter shall be cause for
revocation of any license, certificate or permit issued to such violator or
offending party by the City.
(Ord. 5985-1981. Passed 6-8-81.)

1303.01 CODE ADOPTED; IDENTITY AND PURPOSE.
   Pursuant to the provisions of Ohio R.C. 731.231, the 1959 Edition of the
Regional Building Code, as prepared and promulgated by the Regional Planning
Commission, Cleveland, Ohio, is hereby adopted by the City of Brook Park and
incorporated by reference as a part of the City Building Code as if fully set
out herein, except such provisions as may hereafter be amended, enacted or
repealed. The purpose of the Regional Building Code, as adopted herein, is to
establish uniform standard provisions to govern the construction, alteration,
repair, maintenance, design, materials, equipment and removal or demolition of
all buildings and other structures within the City so as to make them safe and
sanitary for their intended use and occupancy, except that the Code shall not
apply to one and two-family dwellings, and private garages and other structures
appurtenant to such dwellings.
1303.02 FILE AND SALE COPIES.
   A complete copy of the Regional Building Code, as adopted herein, is on file
with the Council Clerk and the Director of Public Service for inspection by the
public, and a copy is also on file in the Cuyahoga County Law Library. The
Council Clerk and the Director of Public Service have copies available for
distribution to the public at cost.
1303.03 DEFINITIONS.
   Wherever used in the Regional Building Code, the following terms shall have
the meanings respectively ascribed to them:
   (a)   "Municipality" means the City of Brook Park, Ohio.
   (b)   "Building Official" means the Building Inspector of Brook Park, Ohio.
   (c)   "Board of Building Code Appeals" means the Board of Zoning and
Building Appeals of Brook Park, Ohio.
1303.04 ENFORCEMENT AND RIGHT OF ENTRY.
   The Building Inspector shall enforce the Regional Building Code, as adopted
herein, and all other laws relating to buildings and structures and, in the
discharge of his official duties, shall have authority, upon proper
identification, to enter any building, structure or premises at any reasonable
hour to enforce and ascertain compliance with such Code or law.
1303.05 BRICK FACING.
   (a)   No commercial building shall be constructed unless all exterior walls
visible from the street are completely faced with either brick conforming to
ASTM standard (C-21 (solid brick) or C-652 (hollow brick) or C-1088 (thin
brick), natural stone, architectural concrete masonry units (CMU), approved
concrete panels or an approved masonry, the color and design approved of by the
Planning Commission.
   (b)   The use of standard, concrete masonry units (CMU), sometimes referred
to as cinder block or cement block, visible from the street as exterior
construction material in any building within the City, is hereby prohibited.
   (c)   An addition to an existing building not conforming to divisions (a) or
(b) of this section may be constructed of the same nonconforming materials as
the main building if the Planning Commission determines that the addition would
be more consistent with the objectives of the Zoning Code if it is constructed
of nonconforming materials than it would be if it is constructed of conforming
materials.
(Ord. 4174-1972. Passed 3-21-72; Ord. 8867-2002. Passed 2-6-02.)

1305.01 INSPECTOR'S POWERS AND DUTIES; INSPECTIONS.
   The City Electrical Inspector or his deputies are hereby authorized to
inspect and reinspect all overhead, underground and interior wires and
apparatus conducting electric current for any purpose whatsoever within the
City limits and to make such tests, as they may deem necessary, to ascertain
the condition of the wires, conductors or appliances. The Electrical Inspector
may remove or cause to be removed any existing obstruction, such as laths,
plastering, boarding or partitions, which may hinder a full and complete
inspection of wires, conductors or appliances. When the electrical conductors
or apparatus are found to be unsafe to life or property, he shall notify the
person owning or operating them to place the same in a safe or secure condition
within a reasonable time, but not to exceed ten days. Any person failing or
refusing to repair, change or remove the same within the time stipulated shall
be subject to the penalty hereinafter provided. All electric light and power
companies shall disconnect their service immediately upon notice from the
Electrical Inspector to do so.
   The Electrical Inspector is authorized to stop work on installations by any
person who fails to pay any required fees up«n notice to do so.
(Ord. 4786-1975. Passed 5-12-75. )
1305.02 RIGHT OF ENTRY; INTERFERENCE WITH DUTIES.
   The Electrical Inspector or his deputies shall, so far as may be necessary
for the performance of their duties, upon proper identification, have the right
to enter any building, site or premises. Any person interfering with them in
the performance of their official duties shall be subject to the penalty
provided in this chapter.
(Ord. 4786-1975. Passed 5-12-75. )
1305.03 NATIONAL ELECTRICAL CODE ADOPTED; PURPOSE AND COPIES. (REPEALED)
   (EDITOR'S NOTE: Section 1305.03 was repealed by Ordinance 9295-2006, passed
June 20, 2006.)
1305.04 ELECTRICAL PROVISIONS REPEALED FROM REGIONAL CODES.
   All provisions of the Regional Dwelling House Code and Regional Building
Code relative to electricity or electrical regulations are hereby repealed as
such pertain to the City.
(Ord. 4786-1975. Passed 5-12-75.)
1305.05 REPORTS OF ACCIDENT OR INJURY.
   If any accident or injury occurs, whether resulting in a fatality or not,
the accident or injury shall be immediately reported to the Electrical
Inspector by the person whose equipment was involved in such accident. This
applies to both interior and exterior installations, but excludes portable
appliances.
(Ord. 4786-1975. Passed 5-12-75.)
1305.06 REMOVAL OR ALTERATION OF NOTICES.
   Whoever removes or alters any sticker or notice relative to electrical
inspections or installations shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and subject to
the penalty provided in this chapter.
(Ord. 4786-1975. Passed 5-12-75.)
1305.07 PERMIT FEES.
   A fee shall be charged for each permit for electrical installations. The
amount of the fee shall be determined according to the fee schedule set forth
in Section
1313.04.
(Ord. 4786-1975. Passed 5-12-75.)
1305.08 PERMIT REQUIRED PRIOR TO INSTALLATION; POSTING.
   No person shall install, or cause to be installed, any electrical lighting,
heating or power wiring or equipment without first obtaining a permit from the
City.
(Ord. 4786-1975. Passed 5-12-75.)
1305.09 CONTRACTOR'S LICENSE REQUIRED.
   No person shall undertake to install, reinstall, repair, replace in whole or
in part, reset, re-assemble, move, alter or convert, any proposed or existing
electrical system or any part thereof, unless such person has been duly
licensed by the Building Commissioner to perform such work in compliance with
the provisions and regulations of this chapter, and in accordance with the
requirements hereof. Applicants for a license to engage in or work at the
trade, occupation or business of an electrical contractor shall make
application for license at the office of the Building Commissioner on a form to
be provided by the Commissioner.
(Ord. 4786-1975. Passed 5-12-75.)
1305.10 LICENSE APPLICATION; BOND.
   (a)   Every application for a license shall contain the name of the person
applying for a license and the place of business of the applicant. If the
applicant is a member of a firm, corporation, copartnership, association or any
combination thereof, the application shh.ll contain the names and addresses of
all members or officers, as the case may be and sa h other information as the
Building Commissioner may require, together with a certified copy of the
corporation minutes or other certified evidence showing that the applicant is
duly authorized to represent an act for such business entity in all matters
regulated by this chapter.
(Ord. 4786-1975. Passed 5-12-75.)
   (b)   Every applicant for a license as an electrical contractor shall, upon
approval of application, furnish and file with the Building Commissioner a bond
in the penal sum of ten thousand dollars ($10,000), to be approved as to form
by the Law Director and as to sufficiency by the Mayor, guaranteeing full and
faithful compliance by the applicant with all the provisions and regulations of
this chapter and the City Building Code.
(Ord. 6977-1987. Passed 1-20-87.)
1305.11 LICENSE ISSUANCE AND FEE.
   Upon approval of the application for a license as an electrical contractor
by the Building Commissioner the applicant shall file with the Commissioner the
required bond, properly executed and approved, and shall pay a license fee as
set forth in Section 1311. 05. The applicant shall receive from the Building
Commissioner a license as an electrical contractor entitling him to install,
reinstall, repair, replace in whole or in part, reset, alter, convert and move
the electrical system pursuant to the provisions and regulations of this
chapter within the corporate limits of the City for the current calendar year.
(Ord. 4786-1975. Passed 5-12-75.)
1305.12 LICENSE EXPIRATION AND RENEWAL.
   All electrical contractors licenses and all renewals thereof shall expire on
December 31 of each year. Licenses may be renewed, provided all noncompliance
with or violations of this chapter by the licensee have been remedied, upon
application for renewal thereof to the Building Commissioner on forms provided
by the Commissioner and upon payment of a renewal fee.
(Ord. 4786-1975. Passed 5-12-75. )
1305.13 LICENSE SUSPENSION OR REVOCATION.
   The Building Commissioner may suspend or revoke any license or renewal
thereof issued under the provisions and regulations of this chapter for any of
the following reasons:
   (a)   Misrepresentation of a material fact by the applicant in obtaining a
license or the renewal thereof;
   (b)   Use of a license in obtaining permits for another;
   (c)   Faulty or defective workmanship;
   (d)   Departure from or disregard of plans and specifications filed with the
application for permits;
   (e)   The noncompliance with or violation of any provision or regulation of
this chapter.
(Ord. 4786-1975. Passed 5-12-75. )
1305.14 HEARING OF APPEAL.
   A licensee whose license has been suspended or revoked may appeal such order
of suspension or revocation to the Board of Zoning and Building Appeals. The
appellant may be represented by counsel at his own expense. The Board shall
permit the appellant and the Building Commissioner to call witnesses and
introduce competent testimony pertinent to a hearing of appeal. The appeal
shall be made in writing and filed with the secretary of the Board within
thirty days after receipt of the notice or order.
(Ord. 4786-1975. Passed 5-12-75. )
1305.15 PERMIT FOR ADDITIONS AND ALTERATIONS; UNSAFE CONDITIONS.
   No alterations, additions or extensions shall be made in any electric
installation without first obtaining a permit from the City and submitting the
same for inspection in the same manner as provided for new work.
   The Electrical Inspector is authorized to refuse to issue a permit for any
addition or extension to any wiring system in an unsafe condition. After a
permit is issued, if for any reason the work covered by the permit or any old
work in the building not covered by the permit is found to be in an unsafe
condition, the Electrical Inspector may refuse to issue a certificate of
approval.
   No owner or occupant of any building and no electric light and power company
shall have connections made or connect to any building without having such
certificate of approval or written permission from the Electrical Inspector. If
additions and alterations have been made to an installation already connected
within a building, the owner or occupant of such building and the electric
light and power company shall disconnect their service immediately upon notice
to do so.
(Ord. 4786-1975. Passed 5-12-75. )
1305.16 INSPECTION PRIOR TO COVERING WORK.
   When the wiring or electrical equipment in any building is being altered or
installed, no person shall cover such wiring or equipment or cause the same to
be covered until the Electrical Inspector or a deputy shall have inspected and
approved the wiring and equipment. The Electrical Inspector or a deputy, after
inspection and approval, shall post a notice in a conspicuous part of the
building, declaring that the wiring or equipment is approved and may be
covered. In interpreting this rule for all work, the contractor shall request
inspection when parts of the work are to be covered, such as for concrete work
where partial inspection is necessary. (Ord. 4786-1975. Passed 5-12-75. )
1305.17 FINAL INSPECTION; SEALED SWITCH.
   Prior to the introduction of electric current into any electric installation
within the City, the Electrical Inspector, upon notification, shall make or
cause to be made a final inspection of the installation. No electric current
shall be introduced into the electrical installation without permission'from
the Electrical Inspector. However, electric light and power companies may
connect their service lines to an installation through an open switch which
shall be so sealed that it shall be impossible to close it without breaking the
seal. No person, other than the Electrical Inspector or his deputies, shall
break the seal, or first close the switch under the penalty provided by this
chapter. A tag setting forth this offense and penalty shall be attached to the
switch.
(Ord. 4786-19.7.5. Passed 5-12-75. )

1305.99 PENALTY.
   (a)   The owner of any premises, building or structure or part thereof where
anything in violation of this chapter shall exist or be placed and any person
who shall violate any of the provisions of this chapter or be employed to
assist in such violation, and all persons who shall fail to comply therewith or
with any regulation thereof, shall, for each and every such violation or
noncompliance, be imprisoned for a definite term or fined, or both, which terms
of imprisonment and fine shall be fixed by the court as provided in this
section.
   (b)   For a first offense the violator is guilty of a misdemeanor of the
second degree.
   (c)   For a second or subsequent offense within one year after the first
offense, the violator is guilty of a misdemeanor of the first degree.
   (d)   Terms of imprisonment for misdemeanors shall be imposed as follows:
      (1)   For a misdemeanor of the first degree, not more than six months.
      (2)   For a misdemeanor of the second degree, not more than ninety days.
   (e)   Fines for misdemeanors shall be imposed as follows:
      (1)   For a misdemeanor of the first degree, not more than one thousand
dollars ($1000) .
      (2)   For a misdemeanor of the second degree, not more than seven hundred
fifty dollars ($750. 00).
(Ord. 4786-1975. Passed 5-12-75. )
CHAPTER 1307
Incinerators; Burning Refuse
1307.01   No incinerators in new apartments or commercial buildings.
1307.02   Existing incinerators compliance.

1307.05   One and two-family residences.

   CROSS REFERENCES
   Waste disposal, burning - see Ohio R.C. Ch. 3734
   Air pollution - see BLDG. Ch.
1341
1307.01 NO INCINERATORS IN NEW APARTMENTS OR COMMERCIAL BUILDINGS.
   No incinerator shall be constructed in or used in conjunction with any
multi-family, apartment, office or commercial building erected in the City
after April 1, 1973.
(Ord. 4931-1976. Passed 5-24-76.)
1307.02 EXISTING INCINERATORS COMPLIANCE.
   The use of any existing incinerator in or used in conjunction with any
multi-family, apartment, office or commercial building shall, after April 1,
1973, comply with the standards and regulations hereinafter set forth in this
chapter.
(Ord. 4931-1976. Passed 5-24-76.)
1307.03 ABATEMENT.
   Any existing incinerator may at any time be shut down and the firing door
padlocked and chained, sealed and tagged for lack of proper repairs,
maintenance or operation by order of the Fire Prevention Bureau or Building
Commissioner.
(Ord. 4931-1976. Passed 5-24-76.)
1307.04 REGULATIONS; ANNUAL PERMIT.
   Any existing incinerator in any zoning use district that is not prohibited
by this chapter, or any new incinerator installation that would be permitted by
this chapter, shall comply with the following minimum standards and
regulations. Existing incinerators shall have a period ending April 1, 1973 to
meet these requirements, provided that the owner or manager of every
commercial, office, multi-family or apartment building having an incinerator
shall, on or before September 1, 1973, submit plans to the Building
Commissioner for the remodeling or alteration of such incinerator in order to
comply with all of the applicable provisions of this chapter. At such time and
every year thereafter the owner or manager of such building shall apply for an
annual permit for the operation of an incinerator from the Commissioner.
   (a)   Every incinerator shall be multiple chambered. The chamber shall be
designed to reduce the velocity of the products of combustion and to promote
the burning of unburned combustible materials before they are released into the
atmosphere.
   (b)   The installer, designer or manufacturer of any new or replacement
equipment shall certify in writing to the City that the incinerator is designed
so that it will not emit smoke into the atmosphere of an appearance, density or
shade darker than number one of the Ringlemann Chart, which chart is published
by the Bureau of Mines, U.S. Department of Interior, August 1955, a copy of
which "Ringlemann Smoke Chart" is attached to original Ordinance 4931-1976,
passed May 24, 1976. The installer shall also certify to the City that a survey
of the premises has been made and that the incinerator is of a type and size
that will dispose of the type and amount of waste produced by the user in
compliance with this section.
   (c)   All incinerators shall be constructed, equipped and operated so as not
to discharge or cause to be discharged into the atmosphere from any refuse
burning, visible emissions of any air contaminant which is darker in shade or
density than that designated as number one on the Ringlemann Chart of the U.S.
Bureau of Mines for more than three minutes in any hour, or of such opacity as
to obscure an observer's view to a degree greater than that designated as
number one of the Ringlemann Chart for Smoke.
   (d)   Every incinerator shall be capable of completely incinerating wet or
dry combustible materials and garbage to ash without causing noisome, offensive
or noxious odors, vapors or gases, and without discharge into the atmosphere of
sparks, flyash or powdered residue of the substance which has been burned; nor
shall any observable smoke, odor or vapor escape from incinerator doors or
joints of any kind into the space containing the equipment.
   (e)   Flue-fed incinerators shall be provided with an automatic ignition
burner which ignites and burns for a predetermined time at regular intervals.
The installation and safety features of this burner shall comply with
nationally recognized good practices.
   (f)   All incinerators permitted by this chapter shall comply with Standard
82 of the National Fire Code of the National Fire Protection Association,
Volume IV, 1970-71, a copy of which is attached to original Ordinance 4931-
1976, passed May 24, 1976.
   (g)   The manufacturers' or designers' operation and maintenance
instructions shall be posted in the vicinity of the incinerator.
   (h)   The incinerator may be shut down for improper operation, malfunction
of any part of the incinerator, poor maintenance, deterioration of any part of
the incinerator or the emission of noisome, offensive or noxious odors, vapors
or gases or the discharge into the atmosphere of sparks, flyash or powdered
residue of the substance which has been burned, upon written notice issued by
the Building Commissioner or Fire Prevention Bureau. The incinerator is not to
be used until all repairs or modifications are made and it has been inspected
and approved for use by the Commissioner. It shall be the responsibility of the
owner or management to see that the above conditions are complied with.
   (i)   No incinerator is to be installed without first making application to,
and gaining approval of the Building Commissioner. If approval is granted, the
Commissioner shall issue the necessary permits after receiving all the
appropriate fees for such permits. The issuance of permits by the Commissioner
shall not be construed as a guarantee of immunity from prosecution or other
legal action for violations occurring after the incinerator is put into
operation.
   (j)   The fire box, grating and ash pit of every incinerator that is in
operation daily shall be cleaned out and emptied once a day. Other incinerators
shall be cleaned out and emptied after use.
   (k)   All electrically activated components shall bear evidence of
Underwriters' Laboratories, Inc. approval.
(Ord. 4931-1976. Passed 5-24-76.)
1307.05 ONE AND TWO-FAMILY RESIDENCES.
   Any new incinerator installation or any replacement incinerator in a single-
family or two-family residence building shall be of the smokeless and odorless
type.
(Ord. 4931-1976. Passed 5-24-76.)
1307.06 BURNING REFUSE.
   No person shall burn any refuse, garbage, rubbish, rubble or material of any
sort for disposal purposes within the City except in an incinerator.
(Ord. 4931-1976. Passed 5-24-76.)
1307.07 SMOKE LIMITS.
   The emission within the City of smoke, the density of which is equal to or
greater than number one of the Ringelmann Chart, published by the Bureau of
Mines, U.S. Department of Interior, from any device or equipment, other than
incinerators, smokestack or chimney of any building, excepting for five minutes
in any one hour, during which time the fire box is cleaned out or a new fire is
being built therein, is declared to be a nuisance and may be summarily abated
by any member of the Police Department or the Fire Department, in addition to
the prosecution and fine provided for in this chapter.
(Ord. 4931-1976. Passed 5-24-76.)
1307.99 PENALTY.
   (a)   Whoever violates any provision of this chapter shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor of the first degree, punishable under Chapter 501 of the Codified
Ordinances.
(Ord. 6025-1981. Passed 8-18-81.)
   (b)   Whoever denies admittance to any officer charged with the enforcement
of this chapter, after proper identification of such officer, or interferes
with any such officer in the performance of his duties under this chapter,
shall be fined not more than fifty dollars ($50.00).
(Ord. 4931-1976. Passed 5-24-76.)

1309.01 DEFINITIONS.
   Wherever used in the Ohio Basic Building Code, the following terms shall
have the meanings respectively ascribed to them:
   (a)   "Municipal Corporation" means the City.
   (b)   "Building Official" means the Building Commissioner of the City except
in references to inspection and approval of plans where the term "Building
Official" means the Plan Examiner for the City.
   (c)   "Local Board of Building Appeals" means the Board of Zoning and
Building Appeals of the City.
(Ord. 6577-1984. Passed 9-18-84.)
1309.02 CURRENT EDITION ADOPTED.
   Pursuant to Ohio R.C. 731.231, there is hereby adopted by and for the
Municipality the current edition of the Ohio Building Code as adopted by the
Ohio Board of Building Standards, Department of Industrial Relations, and as
published in Division 4101:2 of the Ohio Administrative Code, save and except
such portions thereof as may be hereinafter amended or deleted.
(Ord. 9446-2008. Passed 3-18-08.)
1309.025 PURPOSE.
   The purpose of the Ohio Basic Building Code, as adopted in Section
1309.01, is to:
   (a)   Provide uniform minimum standards and requirements for the erection,
construction, repair, alteration and maintenance of buildings, including
construction of industrialized units, such standards relating to the
conservation of energy, safety and sanitation of buildings for their intended
use and occupancy;
   (b)   Formulate such standards and requirements, so far as is practical, in
terms of performance objectives, so as to make adequate performance for the use
intended the test of acceptability;
   (c)   Permit, to the fullest extent feasible, the use of materials and
technical methods, devices and improvements, including the use of
industrialized units, which tend to reduce the cost of construction and
erection without affecting minimum requirements for the health, safety and
security of the occupants or users of buildings or industrialized units and
without preferential treatment of types or classes of materials or products or
methods of construction; and
   (d)   Encourage, so far as may be practical, the standardization of
construction practices, methods, equipment, material and techniques, including
methods employed to produce industrialized units.
(OAC 4101:2-1-05)
1309.03 APPLICATION.
   The Ohio Basic Building Code applies to all buildings except as follows:
   (a)   Single-family, two-family and three-family dwelling houses which are
not constructed of industrialized units, except for the energy conservation
provisions required in "Chapter 13, Energy Conservation" of the Ohio Basic
Building Code (see Ohio R.C. 3781.06, 3781.181 and 3781.182);
   (b)   Buildings owned by and used for a function of the United States
government;
   (c)   Existing buildings where their location, parts, equipment and other
items do not constitute a serious hazard, unless otherwise regulated by the
provisions of "Chapter 34, Existing Structures" of the Ohio Basic Building
Code;
   (d)   Buildings constructed in accordance with plans which have been
approved prior to the effective date of the Ohio Basic Building Code;
   (e)   Buildings or structures which are incident to the use for agricultural
purposes of the land on which said buildings or structures are located,
provided such buildings or structures are not used in the business of retail
trade. For the purposes of this section, a building or structure is not
considered used in the business of retail trade if fifty percent or more of the
gross income received from sales of products in the building or structure by
the owner or operator is from sales of products produced or raised in a normal
crop year on farms owned or operated by the seller (see Ohio R.C. 3781.06 and
3781.061);
   (f)   Agricultural labor camps as defined in Ohio R.C. 3733.41;
   (g)   Single-family, two-family and three-family detached dwelling houses
for which applications have been submitted to the Ohio Director of Human
Services pursuant to Ohio R.C. 5104.03 for the purposes of operating type A
family day-care homes as defined in Ohio R.C. 5104.01;
   (h)   Buildings or structures which are designed, constructed and maintained
in accordance with Federal standards and regulations and are used primarily for
Federal and State military purposes where the U.S. Secretary of Defense,
pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 2233(a)(1), (5) and (6) and 2237, has:
      (1)   Acquired, by purchase, lease or transfer, and constructs, expands,
rehabilitates or corrects and equips, such buildings or structures as he or she
determines to be necessary to carry out the purposes of Chapter 133 of the
U.S.C.;
      (2)   Contributed to the State of Ohio such amounts for the acquisition,
construction, expansion, rehabilitation and conversion by the State of Ohio of
such additional buildings or structures as he or she determines to be required
because of the failure of existing facilities to meet the purposes of Chapter
133 of the U.S.C.; or
      (3)   Contributed to the State of Ohio such amounts for the construction,
alteration or rehabilitation of arms storage rooms as he or she determines to
be required to meet a change in U.S. Department of Defense standards relating
to the safekeeping of arms.
(OAC 4101:2-1-09)
1309.04 FILE AND SALE COPIES.
   A complete copy of the Ohio Basic Building Code, as adopted herein, is on
file with the Clerk of Council for inspection by the public. Copies are
available for distribution to the public at cost from the Banks-Baldwin Law
Publishing Company, Cleveland, Ohio.
(Ord. 6577-1984. Passed 9-18-84.)
1309.05 ENFORCEMENT.
   (a)   The Building Commissioner shall enforce the Ohio Basic Building Code,
as adopted herein, and all other laws relating to buildings and structures,
and, in the discharge of his official duties, shall have authority, upon proper
identification, to enter any building, structure or premises at any reasonable
hour to enforce and ascertain compliance with such Code or Law.
(Ord. 6577-1984. Passed 9-18-84.)
   (b)   Chapters 4101:2-1 to 4101:2-51 of the Ohio Administrative Code,
collectively known as the "Ohio Basic Building Code", shall apply and be
enforced within the City.
(Ord. 6580-1984. Passed 9-18-84.)
1309.06 CONFLICT OF LAWS.
   (a)   Whenever a provision of the Ohio Basic Building Code, as adopted in
Section
1309.02, conflicts with a provision of the Ohio Fire Code or any other order,
standard or rule of the Ohio Department of Commerce, Division of State Fire
Marshal, the provision of the Ohio Basic Building Code shall control, except
that rules adopted and orders issued by the Fire Marshal pursuant to Ohio R.C.
Chapter 3743 prevail in the event of a conflict.
(OAC 4101:2-1-04(B); ORC 3781.11(B))
   (b)   Whenever a provision of the Ohio Basic Building Code, as adopted in
Section
1309.02, conflicts with a provision of any other standard technical code
adopted by the Municipality, other than as provided in subsection (a) hereof,
or any ordinance, resolution, rule or regulation of Council, the stricter
standard shall prevail.
   (c)   When a special provision is made in a use group classification of the
Ohio Basic Building Code and is inconsistent with a general provision of the
Ohio Basic Building Code relating to buildings generally, the special provision
governs, unless it appears that the provisions are cumulative.
(OAC 4101:2-1-07)
1309.99 PENALTY; EQUITABLE REMEDIES.
   (a)   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter, including any provision of the Ohio Basic Building Code adopted in
Section
1309.02, is guilty of a misdemeanor of the first degree and shall be fined not
more than one thousand dollars ($1,000) or imprisoned not more than six months,
or both, for each offense. Unless otherwise provided, a separate offense shall
be deemed committed each day during or on which a violation or noncompliance
occurs or continues.
   (b)   The application of the penalty provided in subsection (a) hereof shall
not be deemed to prevent the enforced removal of prohibited conditions, or the
application of any other equitable remedy.

1310.01 2004 OBOA ONE, TWO, AND THREE FAMILY DWELLING CODE ADOPTED; PURPOSES.
   Pursuant to the provisions of Ohio R.C. 731.231, the 2004 OBOA One, Two, and
Three Family Dwelling Code is hereby adopted as the Brook Park Building Code as
if fully set out herein, except such provisions as are hereinafter amended,
enacted, deleted or repealed. The purposes of the Ohio Building Officials
Association One, Two and Three Family Dwelling Code, as adopted herein, are to
provide increased uniformity across the State, improved communication and
understanding of the Code and accessibility of Code changes to all Ohio
jurisdictions, as well as to provide a model set of minimum construction
standards to safeguard the life, health and public welfare of the citizens of
the City.
(Ord. 8900-2002. Passed 5-21-02; Ord. 9097-2004. Passed 5-18-04.)
1310.02 FILE AND SALE COPIES.
   A complete copy of the OBOA One, Two, and Three Family Dwelling Code, as
adopted herein, is on file with the Building Department for inspection by the
public. The Building Department also has copies available for distribution to
the public, at cost.
(Ord. 8900-2002. Passed 5-21-02.)
1310.03 ENFORCEMENT; RIGHT OF ENTRY.
   The Building Commissioner or his or her duly authorized representatives,
shall enforce the OBOA One, Two, and Three Family Dwelling Code, as adopted
herein, and all other laws relating to buildings and structures, and, in the
discharge of his or her official duties, shall have authority, upon proper
identification, to enter any dwelling, building, structure or premises at any
reasonable hour to enforce and ascertain compliance with such Code or law.
(Ord. 8900-2002. Passed 5-21-02.)
1310.04 AMENDMENTS.
   The OBOA One, Two and Three Family Dwelling Code, as adopted herein, is
hereby revised by as follows:
   (a)   Plywood Roof Sheathing. All plywood roof sheathing shall be not less
than one- half inch thick.
   (b)   Surface Drainage (Amended). Positive drainage shall be provided for
each lot or plot by proper draining so that a nuisance will not be created.
Catch basins or properly connected under-drains shall be installed, or other
approved provisions made where water may pocket, to preclude the accumulation
of surface water. Regrading shall be done so that existing natural ground
drainage of the surround area shall not be impeded. Front yard surface drainage
shall be obtained by grading from the building line to the curb or roadside
ditch. The slope shall be downward from the building line at the rate of three-
eights inch vertical per foot horizontal. The front yard grade shall be set
from the established grade of the street and shall be measured from the
centerline of streets without curbs, and from the top of the face of the curb
where such exists.
   (c)   Factory-Built Fireplace Stoves.
      (1)   Factory-built fireplace stoves shall bear the label of an approved
testing laboratory and shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's
instructions.
      (2)   Hearth extensions shall be provided in accordance with subsection
(m)(2) hereof and the manufacturer's instructions.
   (d)   Smoke Detector. One approved, listed and labeled smoke detector
sensing visible or invisible particles of combustion shall be installed in the
same room as each unit and in a manner and location consistent with its
listing. When actuated, the detector shall provide an alarm suitable to warn
the occupants with the dwelling.
   (e)   Backfill Over Footing Drains. Backfill over footing drains shall be
pervious material of the type and size required for the particular type of
drain construction being used and shall be carried up to 12 inches of the
established surface grade. The top 12 inches of the backfill shall consist of
six inches of an impervious clay soil, topped with six inches of topsoil if the
surface is to be covered with lawn or shrubs. If the surface adjacent to the
foundation wall is to be paved or have similar treatment, then the backfill
near the top may be suitable base for such construction.
(Ord. 8900-2002. Passed 5-21-02.)
1310.05 CONFLICTS OF LAWS.
   In the event of a conflict between any of the provisions of the OBOA One,
Two, and Three Family Dwelling Code, as adopted in Section
1310.01, and a provision of any other technical code adopted by the City by
reference, which pertains to one and two-family dwellings, the higher or
stricter standard shall control.
(Ord. 8900-2002. Passed 5-21-02.)

or both, for each offense. Unless otherwise provided, a separate offense shall
be deemed committed each day during or on which a violation or noncompliance
occurs or continues.
   (b)   The application of the penalty provided in division (a) of this
section shall not be deemed to prevent the enforced removal of prohibited
conditions, or the application of any other equitable remedy.

1311.01 CONTRACTOR DEFINED.
    "Contractor", as used in this chapter, means any individual, firm,
copartnership, corporation, association or other organization, or any
combination of any thereof, who or which by himself or itself, or by or through
others, constructs, alters, repairs, adds to, subtracts from, reconstructs or
remodels any building, structure or appurtenance thereto, or who or which
undertakes or offers to undertake, or purports to have the capacity to
undertake, or submits a bid so to do. The term "contractor" includes
subcontractor and specialty contractor, whose operations as such are the
performance of construction work requiring special skill and whose principal
contracting business involves the use of specialized building trades or crafts.
(Ord. 1854-1958. Passed 10-7-58; Ord. 9604-2009. Passed 8-18-09.)
1311.02 REGISTRATION REQUIRED; EXCEPTIONS.
   (a)   No person, firm or corporation shall engage in the business or act in
the capacity of a contractor, as herein defined, except pursuant to a
registration issued in conformity with the provisions of this chapter by the
Building Commissioner.
   (b)   No provision of this chapter shall be interpreted to require that the
owner of a one or two-family dwelling or individual row house shall be
registered to personally perform work upon the premises occupied or to be
occupied by the owner thereof as such owner's established residence.
(Ord. 8611-1999. Passed 11-16-99; Ord. 9604-2009. Passed 8-18-09.)
1311.03 WORK PERMIT TO BE ISSUED ONLY TO APPLICANT.
   No permit required by the provisions of the City Building Code shall be
issued for work to be undertaken by contract except to a registered contractor.
(Ord. 1854-1958. Passed 10-7-58; Ord. 9604-2009. Passed 8-18-09.)
1311.04 APPLICATION AND QUALIFICATIONS.
   Application for such certificate of qualification shall be made on forms
provided by the Building Commissioner and shall set forth the name of the
applicant, his age, his place of business, his experience in the work for which
a registration is applied and such other information as the Commissioner may
require in order to determine the qualifications of such applicant for the work
proposed to be done under such certificate. The Commissioner, in determining
whether the applicant is qualified to receive the certificate applied for, may
grant such certificate upon finding that the applicant has been duly licensed
by any other testing community or the State, if the Commissioner is satisfied
that an adequate investigation or examination has been made by such
municipality of the applicant's qualifications for the work for which such
certificate was issued.
   (a)   The applicant shall have a minimum of three years practical experience
and an affidavit to this effect shall be provided.
   (b)   The applicant shall provide any and all references as may be requested
on the application form in the manner provided.
   (c)   If the applicant's work or work done under the applicant (as a general
contractor) includes plumbing, electrical or gas installation, any installer
working in the City of Brook Park shall have the following:
      (1)   A valid certificate of qualification from the City of Cleveland,
(formally called Journeyman Plumbers License), or Electrician, or HVAC Fuel/Gas
Installer, which ever is applicable;
      (2)   A valid Journeyman Plumbers, Electricians, HVAC/Gas Installer
License from a municipality or county in Ohio that required a comprehensive
examination, whichever is applicable;
      (3)   Proof of passing the Exterior "Plumbing with Gas" examination
(Columbus version).
   (d)   Violators of this provision will be issued a notice and immediately
removed from the work site. A second offense will result in a three-year ban
from working on any of the plumbing, electrical or HVAC/Fuel Gas work in the
City of Brook Park.
   (e)   Apprentices registered with the Ohio State Apprenticeship Council are
exempt from this section.
(Ord. 8611-1999. Passed 11-16-99; Ord. 9131-2004. Passed 9-7-04; Ord. 9604-
2009. Passed 8-18-09.)
1311.05 REGISTRATION FEE AND TERM.
   Upon being satisfied that the applicant is qualified and able to
satisfactorily do the work for which a registration is applied, the Building
Commissioner shall issue a registration to the applicant upon the payment of a
fee of one hundred twenty-five dollars ($125.00). The registration shall expire
on December 31 of the year of issue and may be renewed annually thereafter upon
the payment of an annual renewal fee of one hundred twenty-five dollars
($125.00).
(Ord. 8611-1999. Passed 11-16-99; Ord. 9604-2009. Passed 8-18-09.)
1311.06 SURETY BOND AND INSURANCE REQUIRED.
   (a)   Prior to the issuance of a registration, the Building Commissioner
shall require an applicant to furnish a surety bond, to be approved as to form
by the Director of Law and as to sufficiency by the Mayor, guaranteeing full
and faithful compliance by the applicant with all the provisions and
regulations of the City Building Code, and binding the surety thereon to
correct or abate any violations of the City Building Code whenever the
applicant named as principal on such bond refuses, neglects or fails to correct
or abate such violation within a reasonable time limit as set by the Building
Commissioner. The bond shall indemnify the City and all other persons from
injuries or damages arising by reason of the applicant's negligence or failure
to properly perform any work undertaken pursuant to such license. The bond for
all contractors shall be in the penal sum of forty thousand dollars ($40,000).
   (b)   In addition to the bond required by subsection (a) hereof, every
contractor shall, as a condition of any registration issued pursuant to this
chapter, maintain Contractor's Comprehensive General and Automobile Liability
insurance, or its equivalent, extended (or by means of a separate policy) to
include liability for damage caused by explosion, collapse, underground,
independent contractors, products and completed operations, together with
owner's protective liability, with not less than the policy limits set forth in
subsection (c) hereof. Such policy or policies of insurance shall name the City
of Brook Park as an additional insured for all work performed within the
corporate limits of the City, and shall contain the following special
provision: "The Company agrees that ten days prior to cancellation, material
alteration or reduction of the insurance afforded by this policy, with respect
to the license involved, written notice shall be sent by certified mail to the
City of Brook Park." An exact copy of such policy or policies shall be
deposited with the Building Commissioner prior to the expiration date of any of
the initial insurances. All insurance herein specified shall be with a company
authorized to do business in the State of Ohio and acceptable to the
Commissioner.
    (c)   The policy or policies of insurance required by subsection (b) hereof
shall:
      (1)   Have a policy limit for bodily injury and property damage of not
less than one million dollars ($1,000,000) for each occurrence, if the
contractor engages in the construction, reconstruction, maintenance or repair
of any of the public highways, streets, avenues, alleys, sidewalks, public
grounds, bridges, aqueducts and viaducts within the corporate limits of the
City; or
      (2)   Have a policy limit for bodily injury and property damage of not
less than three hundred thousand dollars ($300,000) for each occurrence, if the
contractor does not engage in the construction, reconstruction, maintenance or
repair of any of the public highways, streets, avenues, alleys, sidewalks,
public grounds, bridges, aqueducts and viaducts within the corporate limits of
the City.
    (d)   If an applicant's policy or policies of insurance, as required by
subsection (b) hereof, have policy limits less than those specified in
subsection (c)(1) hereof, the registration issued to such applicant shall
contain the following endorsement in a conspicuous location on the face
thereof: "THIS REGISTRATION IS NOT VALID FOR ANY WORK INVOLVING THE
CONSTRUCTION, RECONSTRUCTION, MAINTENANCE OR REPAIR OF ANY OF THE PUBLIC
HIGHWAYS, STREETS, AVENUES, ALLEYS, SIDEWALKS, PUBLIC GROUNDS, BRIDGES,
AQUEDUCTS AND VIADUCTS WITHIN THE CORPORATE LIMITS OF THE CITY OF BROOK PARK."
(Ord. 8611-1999. Passed 11-16-99; Ord. 9604-2009. Passed 8-18-09; Ord. 11443-
2024. Passed 11-19-24.)
1311.07 REGISTRATION SUSPENSION OR REVOCATION.
   The Building Commissioner may suspend or revoke any registration issued
under the provisions of this chapter for any of the following reasons:
   (a)   Misrepresentation of a material fact by the applicant in obtaining a
license or renewal thereof;
   (b)   Use of a registration in obtaining permits for another person;
   (c)   Faulty or defective workmanship;
   (d)   Departure from or disregard of plans and specifications filed with the
application for a permit;
   (e)   The noncompliance with or violation of any provision of the City
Building Code.
(Ord. 8611-1999. Passed 11-16-99; Ord. 9604-2009. Passed 8-18-09.)
1311.08 HEARING OF APPEAL.
   A contractor whose registration has been suspended or revoked may appeal
such order of suspension or revocation to the Board of Zoning and Building
Appeals. The appellant may be represented by counsel at his own expense. The
Board shall permit the appellant and the Building Commissioner to call
witnesses and introduce competent testimony pertinent to a hearing of appeal.
The appeal shall be made in writing and filed with the secretary of the Board
within 30 days after the receipt of the notice or order. The Board may affirm,
reverse or modify any action taken by the Building Commissioner.
(Ord. 8611-1999. Passed 11-16-99; Ord. 9604-2009. Passed 8-18-09.)

1311.99 PENALTY.
   (a)   Where work for which a permit is required by this chapter is started
prior to obtaining such permit, the fees required by such permit shall be
doubled, but the payment of such double fee shall not relieve any person from
fully complying with the lawful requirements of any Ohio statute or City
ordinance.
    (b)   Whoever violates any provision of this chapter or fails to comply
with any order issued pursuant thereto shall be guilty of a misdemeanor of the
first degree, punishable under
Chapter 501 of the Codified Ordinances.
(Ord. 6025-1981. Passed 8-18-81; Ord. 9604-2009. Passed 8-18-09.)

1313.01 GENERAL PROVISIONS.
   Except as otherwise specifically provided for, the following provisions
shall prevail in the issuance of all types of permits. The Director of Public
Service and/or Building Commissioner, before issuing any permit, are authorized
to charge and collect the fees specified in this chapter. The fees prescribed
herein shall be additive and, unless otherwise specifically provided, separate
fees shall be paid for each of the items listed. All fees shall be computed and
determined by the Director of Public Service and/or Building Commissioner, who
shall give a receipt for cash payment. Fees for plan examination shall be
separate and paid directly to the Plan Examiner or Alternate Plan Examiner, who
shall give a receipt for cash payment.
(Ord. 6578-1984. Passed 9-18-84.)
1313.015 SUBCONTRACTOR REQUIREMENT.
   (a)   At the time of applying for a building permit of any kind, every
contractor, general or subcontractor, must submit a list of all subcontractors
who will be working under such permit.
   (b)   If at any time during the construction of the work provided for by the
permit, there is a change in subcontractors to any contractor, or
subcontractor, such change shall be reported within twenty-four hours by such
contractor or subcontractor, to the Building Department.
(Ord. 4244-1972. Passed 6-20-72.)
1313.016 PERMIT REVIEW PERIOD.
   The Building Commissioner shall have forty-eight working hours in which to
review plans and/or specifications for any type of construction not regulated
by the Ohio Basic Building Code and requiring a permit within the City before
he shall be required to issue a permit for such construction. The Plan Examiner
or Alternate Plan Examiner will begin the review of all construction plans
regulated by the Ohio Basic Building Code within twenty- four working hours
after receiving the plans and will recommend to the Building Commissioner,
either the issuance or refusal of permits required for the construction. The
review time for construction plans regulated by the Ohio Basic Building Code
will vary depending on the complexity of the problem.
(Ord. 6578-1984. Passed 9-18-84.)
1313.017 PERMIT REVIEW FOR FLOOD DAMAGE.
   The Building Commissioner shall review all building permit applications for
new construction or substantial improvements to determine whether proposed
building sites will be reasonably safe from flooding. If a proposed building
site is in a location that has a flood hazard, any proposed new construction or
substantial improvement, including prefabricates and mobile homes, must:
   (a)   Be designed, or modified, and anchored to prevent flotation, collapse
or lateral movement of the structure.
   (b)   Use construction materials and utility equipment that are resistant to
flood damage
   (c)   Use construction methods and practices that will minimize flood
damage.
(Ord. 4766-1975. Passed 4-1-75. )
1313.018 SUBDIVISION REVIEW.
   The Building Commissioner shall review subdivision proposals and other
proposed new developments to assure that:
   (a)   All such proposals are consistent with the need to minimize flood
damage.
   (b)   All public utilities and facilities, such as sewer, gas, electrical
and water systems are located, elevated and constructed to minimize or
eliminate flood damage.
   (c)   Adequate drainage is provided so as to reduce exposure to flood
hazards.
(Ord. 4766-1975. Passed 4-1-75.)
1313.019 WATER, SEWER SYSTEM DESIGN.
   The Building Commissioner shall require new or replacement water supply
systems and/or sanitary sewage systems to be designed to minimize or eliminate
infiltration of flood waters, and require on-site waste disposal systems to be
located so as to avoid impairment of them or contamination from them during
flooding.
(Ord. 4766-1975. Passed 4-1-75. )
1313.02 GRADING OF BUILDINGS.
   For the purpose of computing fees to be charged for the issuance of building
permits, all buildings, structures and appurtenances shall be graded as
follows:
   (a)   Grade 1. The first grade includes public buildings designed to be
occupied by State, County or City administration offices (United States
government buildings are regarded as belonging to this grade, but are deemed to
be outside of the jurisdiction of the City Building Code); courtrooms;
libraries; museums; art galleries; public or private hospitals; schools and
colleges or other buildings containing class, drawing or lecture rooms for the
purpose of education or instruction; music halls; churches; convention halls;
auditoriums; assembly halls or that part of any building containing assembly
rooms for a concourse of more than one hundred people; theaters; opera houses;
playhouses; pavilions, and public utility buildings.
   (b)   Grade 2. The second grade includes hotels, motels or restaurants, or
any building or part thereof designed to be used for supplying food or shelter;
office buildings designed or used for office purposes in the conduct of general
business, but may have a store or salesroom on the ground floor, and no part of
such building shall be used for living purposes except for the janitor and his
family; store buildings designed or used for the sale of merchandise or objects
of utility or general supply; factories arid workshops or any other building
designed or used for the manufacture of merchandise by machinery or hand;
warehouses, and gasoline service stations.
   (c)   Grade 3. The third grade includes tenement houses, apartments, row
houses and other buildings containing suites or apartments used for permanent
habitation by more than two families; clubhouses, and other buildings used or
intended to be used by an organization or society for mutual entertainment or
recreation.
   (d)   Grade 4. The fourth grade includes dwellings which are used or
designed and intended to be used as the home or residence of not more than two
separate and distinct families, and includes the part of all buildings used by
one family having another grade of occupancy either above or below or adjacent
to the residential part of the building.
   (e)   Grade 5. The fifth grade includes garages; buildings designed or used
for public livery or boarding stables; private barns, sheds, pens or coops;
slaughterhouses, and any building for the feeding or sheltering of animals or
fowl.
   (f)   Grade 6. The sixth grade includes all buildings, structures and
appurtenances not otherwise included in another grade, and includes fences,
signs and billboards.
(Ord. 726. Passed 6-13-32.)

1313.07 OBSTRUCTION DEPOSIT.
   (a)   To protect the City property from damage, to ensure the completion of
all construction work, the removal of temporary offices, tools and/or storage
sheds, and the satisfactory restoration of the property involved, a deposit is
required, prior to issuance of a building permit, on all new dwellings,
commercial construction or any construction deemed necessary by the Building
Commissioner.
      (1)   On every new dwelling, a minimum cash deposit of five hundred
dollars ($500.00) shall be required.
      (2)   For group building of dwellings by one contractor, for commercial
construction or any other type of construction, the amount of the cash deposit
shall be set by the Building Commissioner in an amount he deems adequate to the
particular circumstances.
      (3)   All deposits shall be subject to increase if the nature of the work
so warrants.
   (b)   When all construction work is completed, all temporary office, tool
and/or storage sheds are removed, and when the property involved has been
restored to a reasonable state of orderliness, then a final inspection shall be
made.
      (1)   Where work has been completed satisfactorily at the time of final
inspection, any cash deposits shall be refunded, except for any charges deemed
necessary for extra inspections.
      (2)   If the work is not satisfactorily completed within a specified time
given by the Building Commissioner in writing, the entire amount of the cash
deposit shall be forfeited.
(Ord. 7026-1987. Passed 6-16-87; Ord. 9546-2008. Passed 12-16-08.)
1313.08 HOME IMPROVEMENT MONTHS; WAIVER OF BUILDING PERMIT FEES.
   (a)   The months of June, July and August, 2000, and every year thereafter,
until duly changed by Council, are hereby designated Home Improvement Months in
the City of Brook Park.
   (b)   The action of the City's administration is hereby ratified in
providing for a waiver of fees for building permits for residential improvement
and maintenance projects on three-family, two-family and one-family homes in
the City of Brook Park during the months of June, July and August, 2000, and
every year thereafter until duly changed by Council.
   (c)   The Director of Public Safety is hereby designated as the
administrative official who shall promulgate the issuance of rules and
regulations for the implementation of this program. Said rules and regulations
are attached to original Resolution 11-2000, passed May 16, 2000, marked
Exhibit "A," and made a part hereof as if fully rewritten herein.
(Res. 11-2000. Passed 5-16-00.)
1313.99 PENALTY.
   (a)   Where work for which a permit is required by this chapter is started
prior to obtaining such permit, the fees required by such permit shall be
doubled, but the payment of such double fee shall not relieve any person from
fully complying with the lawful requirements of any Ohio statute or City
ordinance.
     (b)   Any person, whether as principal, agent, employee or otherwise, who
violates any provision of this chapter or fails to comply with any order issued
pursuant thereto, shall be imprisoned for a definite term, or fined, or both,
which term of imprisonment and fine shall be fixed by the court as provided in
this section.
   (c)   Each day of existence of any continued violation shall be deemed a
separate offense.
   (d)   For each offense, the violator is guilty of permit and inspection fee
violation, a misdemeanor of the fourth degree.
   (e)   Terms of imprisonment shall be imposed for a misdemeanor of the fourth
degree, not more than thirty days.
   (f)   Fines shall be imposed for a misdemeanor of the fourth degree, not
more than two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00).
(Ord. 4560-1974. Passed 3-19-74.)
